target.title: fix(gateway): cap sessions.compact maxLines
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines N` accepts an unbounded `N`. The CLI parses it with `parseStrictPositiveIntOrUndefined` (no maximum; `src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.ts:432`) and forwards it to the `sessions.compact` gateway RPC. The gateway handler (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-compact.ts`) only lower-bounds the value:

```ts
Math.max(1, Math.floor(p.maxLines))
```

With `maxLines` set to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (or any value larger than the transcript), `trimSessionTranscriptForManualCompact` in `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.transcript.ts` loads every transcript event, serializes them all, and — because `events.length <= maxLines` — writes nothing useful: an intentional compaction becomes an expensive no-op / memory spike that still pays the full transcript read. There is no ceiling anywhere on the path (CLI parse, TypeBox schema `Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })`, gateway handler, accessor).

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a named constant and clamp at the gateway boundary, the last common point every client (CLI, webchat, SDK) passes through:

```ts
const MAX_COMPACT_MAX_LINES = 100_000;

const maxLines =
  typeof p.maxLines === "number" && Number.isFinite(p.maxLines)
    ? Math.min(Math.max(1, Math.floor(p.maxLines)), MAX_COMPACT_MAX_LINES)
    : undefined;
```

This mirrors the merged `parseDays` day-count cap from #110552 (`MAX_USAGE_DAYS`, clamp-only at the handler, no schema change). The TypeBox schema in `packages/gateway-protocol` is deliberately untouched: clamping keeps the wire contract permissive instead of turning oversized values into validation errors, so older/newer clients keep working. Callers that genuinely want full-history retention are unaffected in intent — they should omit `maxLines` and use model-backed compaction, which is what the no-`maxLines` path already does.

## User Impact

- `openclaw sessions compact <key> --max-lines 9007199254740991` no longer triggers a full-transcript load/rewrite no-op; the effective keep-count is capped at 100,000 lines.
- All previously valid requests (any `maxLines` up to 100k, or omitted) behave exactly as before — the clamp only engages for absurd values that were already no-ops or memory hazards.
- No config, schema, or CLI flag changes; no migration needed.

## Evidence

New regression test in `src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts`:

- `sessions.compact maxLines clamps absurd values to the manual trim cap` — seeds 100,001 SQLite transcript rows through the real accessor (`replaceTranscriptEvents`), then calls the real gateway RPC `sessions.compact` with `maxLines: 1e12`. Asserts `compacted: true`, `kept: 100_000`, an archive marker, and exactly 100,000 retained rows reloaded from the store. Uncapped, the same request would return `compacted: false, kept: 100_001` (the expensive no-op).

Reverse verification (control-red): with the handler change stashed, the new test FAILS (`compacted` is `false`, all 100,001 rows retained — the no-op); with the fix restored it passes. So the test pins the clamp, not incidental behavior.

Test suite:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
```

(21 pre-existing tests plus the new one; all green. The new test is intentionally slower — it seeds and trims 100k real SQLite rows to make the cap observable through the production RPC path.)

tsgo (scoped lanes covering both touched files):

```
$ pnpm tsgo:core        # exit 0
$ pnpm tsgo:core:test   # exit 0
```

Lint / formatting:

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-compact.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts   # exit 0
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <both files>   # all matched files use the correct format
$ git diff --check   # clean
```

Diff stat:

```
 src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-compact.ts |  7 +++-
 src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts | 51 ++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 57 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

Production change is 4 lines: the `MAX_COMPACT_MAX_LINES` constant plus the `Math.min(...)` clamp. No schema, CLI, or accessor changes.

Pattern precedent: #110552 (merged) — named handler-level cap, clamp-only, no stricter validation.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound ci-run-timings git and GitHub CLI operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a git network operation (`git ls-remote`) in the ci-run-timings script could hang indefinitely when the Git remote is unreachable. Without a timeout, the script would block on network I/O until the job timeout, stalling CI timing reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"], ??` call performs a network operation to list remote refs. All network-touching `execFileSync` calls must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #109982 (npm resume GitHub lookups).

## User Impact

CI timing reports can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when the Git remote is unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ??)` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/ci-run-timings.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325) and `scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` (#109968).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ...])` call, injected a `git` shim that blocks on `ls-remote` forever, and verified the script exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-ci-run-timings-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: getRemoteMainSha() via execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"])
fixture: git ls-remote waits forever
timeout: CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: git ls-remote origin main
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached.

target.title: fix(process): trim UTF-8 boundary on win32 in truncated command output
target.body:
## Problem

`trimTruncatedUtf8Boundary` in `src/process/exec-output.ts` skipped UTF-8 boundary trimming entirely when `process.platform === "win32"`. This left partial UTF-8 code points at the truncation boundary of captured command output, causing `Buffer.toString("utf8")` downstream to emit U+FFFD replacement characters in truncated doctor/cron/plugin command output on Windows.

The win32 skip was introduced in #106495 (Execa refactor) without documented rationale. Node.js stdout is UTF-8 on Windows by default, so the same boundary-trimming logic applies.

## Fix

Remove the `process.platform === "win32"` guard from `trimTruncatedUtf8Boundary` so truncated output is always trimmed on a valid UTF-8 code point boundary, regardless of platform.

- Files changed: 2
- LOC delta: +47 / -2

## Regression proof

New tests in `src/process/exec.test.ts` mock `process.platform` to `"win32"` and verify that `finalizeCapturedOutput`:
- Trims leading continuation bytes in tail mode (emoji split mid-codepoint)
- Trims trailing partial code point in head mode
- Produces no U+FFFD replacement characters

\`\`\`
 ✓ |process| ../../src/process/exec.test.ts (41 tests | 1 skipped) 3598ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed | 1 skipped (41)
\`\`\`

## Risk

Minimal. The fix removes a platform-specific skip that had no documented rationale. The trimming logic is already used on Linux/macOS without issue. On Windows, the only behavioral change is that truncated UTF-8 output no longer contains replacement characters — the output is strictly more correct.

target.title: refactor(macos): move PortGuardian state to SQLite
target.body:
Stacked on #110392. Review and merge after that PR.

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS PortGuardian orphan-tunnel ledger remains in a host-global JSON file even though OpenClaw already ships a canonical SQLite table for the same durable records. JSON read/merge/write coordination can lose tunnel ownership during crashes or concurrent app activity, leaving SSH children occupying local ports without a reliable recovery receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

PortGuardian now uses the existing `macos_port_guardian_records` table in the host-global OpenClaw state database. The logical record shape remains unchanged: `pid`, `port`, `command`, `mode`, and `timestamp`. This is additive at the schema and API boundaries: no table change, schema-version bump, wire-format change, or dual-write path.

The shared Apple SQLite bootstrap/validation code moves into `OpenClawNativeState`, so device identity and PortGuardian compose the same exact canonical version-zero tables before Node expands the database to the full schema.

Legacy `port-guard.json` is a one-time migration input only. Migration snapshots under the shipped Darwin lock, plans process reconciliation outside both the file lock and SQLite transaction, revalidates the exact source, applies a short synchronous transaction, verifies receipts, and retires the JSON file. Runtime then reads and writes SQLite only.

Mixed-version app copies fail closed. A signed storage-capability marker is accepted only when Security.framework metadata matches the running process kernel CDHash. Tunnel launch holds a guardian reservation from completed legacy reconciliation through process spawn and durable receipt commit. Every mutation transaction revalidates the supported schema and canonical table, including retained connections after another process advances the database.

## User Impact

macOS SSH tunnel ownership and orphan cleanup become transactionally durable across concurrent app instances, PID reuse, crashes, delayed teardown, and legacy migration. Fresh installs no longer create the JSON ledger or lock sidecar.

This is a one-way storage cutover. Downgrading afterward to an older JSON-only app does not expose receipts written only to SQLite; rollback requires restoring a compatible backup or upgrading again.

## Maintainer Decision

Approve both deliberate contracts before merge:

1. Native-runtime migration, bounded to interoperability with the shipped Darwin lock and signed mixed-copy detection.
2. One-way downgrade/mixed-version behavior: old JSON-only copies must not share the migrated state directory.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `d4889f49d1dbdb8e9a4f7bc440f81b7387696f7a`, stacked on #110392 at `833680d025ac55c612ca2621a22c4ef92fb535c2`.
- Final rebase range-diff: all 9 PortGuardian commits are patch-identical, including the one-line package-test caller cleanup exposed by hosted `OpenClawKit` compilation.
- Developer-ID-signed candidate proof on the patch-equivalent pre-restack head: released v2026.7.1 had no storage marker; mixed-version exclusion preserved JSON and the live SSH child; one-time migration preserved one exact SQLite receipt; restart was idempotent; orphan recovery killed the child and compare-deleted its receipt. The guest ended `SIGNED_PORTGUARDIAN_PROOF=PASS`, then snapshot restore stopped the VM.
- Current-head TypeScript proof: 87 state-database tests passed with 1 skip, 490 database-first guard tests passed, and 46 device-identity/migration tests passed.
- Final PortGuardian store proof: 21 Swift tests passed, including retained-connection rejection after a newer schema appears. Earlier signed-app scope passed 47 PortGuardian/tunnel tests.
- Prior patch-equivalent remote changed gate passed. Hosted exact-head CI is green: 91 passed checks, 28 intentional skips, and no failure or pending check.
- Full architecture chain, Kysely guardrails, dead-code exports, iOS SwiftFormat, generated baseline, and diff checks pass on the final stack. The final head also passes a focused `OpenClawKit` target build and exact SwiftFormat check.
- Fresh autoreview of the final PortGuardian test-caller cleanup: clean, no accepted/actionable findings, confidence 0.95. The preceding identity caller cleanup was clean at 0.99, PortGuardian tree-delta review at 0.98, stale-schema hardening at 0.96, and identity error-type cleanup at 0.97.

AI assistance was used for implementation and review. Maintainer-directed design, focused tests, signed native behavior proof, and patch-identity checks were performed before handoff.

target.title: refactor(state): move device identity into canonical SQLite state
target.body:
Stacked on #110611. Review and merge after that prerequisite.

Related: #107227

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw still treated `identity/device.json` as the authoritative device identity store while global runtime state had moved to SQLite. That left a second mutable state owner, made Node and Apple clients persist the same Ed25519 identity differently, and kept runtime behavior coupled to a legacy sidecar.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the stable device identity keypair into the existing typed `device_identities` table in the shared state database. Runtime code reads and writes SQLite only. `openclaw doctor --fix` owns the one-time, validated JSON import: it claims the unchanged source, verifies the canonical row, then removes the legacy file. Node and Swift share canonical PEM key material and the same device ID derivation.

Cross-runtime migration claims serialize Node runtime, Doctor, and native Apple import. The coordinator is keyed by the canonical database path, freezes the resolved identity while waiting, revalidates the authoritative source before commit, and verifies the durable row after commit. Aggregate operation and cleanup failures retain both errors.

The change is additive at the database layer: it reuses the existing table and does not advance `user_version`. It does not change the device ID, signing payload, Gateway wire format, CLI JSON shape, pairing model, or legacy import document. Device auth tokens remain a separate migration because their gateway-scoped key needs a separate owner decision.

## User Impact

Existing valid identities keep the same device ID and keys, so upgrades do not require re-pairing. Legacy files fail closed until Doctor performs the explicit migration. Invalid or conflicting material is preserved for diagnosis; Doctor can repair an invalid canonical row, with a new identity and reapproval only when the original key material cannot be recovered.

This is a one-way database-first cutover. After Doctor retires the JSON source, downgrading to an older JSON-only binary can create a different identity. Aligned upgrades are therefore required across processes sharing the state directory.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `833680d025ac55c612ca2621a22c4ef92fb535c2`, stacked on #110611 at `a1fad5d5096410f8f821280dc32f6b82e8ef6699`.
- The head advances the prior reviewed identity stack by four behavior-neutral cleanup commits: test-only wrappers moved out of the app module, the unshipped throw-only error type became a categorized `NSError` factory, package-test callers moved to the canonical internal seam, and the gateway readiness test now pins the TaskLocal state directory used by its SQLite identity. Runtime entry points, localized error messages, and migration behavior are unchanged.
- Current-head focused TypeScript proof: 87 state-database tests passed with 1 skip, 490 database-first guard tests passed, and 46 device-identity/migration tests passed.
- Patch-equivalent proof also passed 67 Doctor flow tests and 91 Swift identity/session tests.
- Prior patch-equivalent Testbox changed gate passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29637761945. Hosted exact-head CI is green: 98 passed checks, 32 intentional skips, and no failure or pending check. The shared dead-code workflow's partial rerun missed an artifact; a full attempt-3 rerun passed both consumer scans and their intersection.
- Full architecture chain, Kysely guardrails, dead-code exports, iOS SwiftFormat, `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check`, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. The identity enum is below the 900-line SwiftLint cap. The final head also passes a focused `OpenClawKit` target build and exact SwiftFormat check.
- Fresh autoreview of the state-isolation cleanup reported one non-actionable claim at 0.92; source verification rejected it because the readiness-failure reset remains immediately before descriptor installation and also in deferred cleanup. The prior caller cleanup was clean at 0.99, error-type cleanup at 0.97, test-API cleanup at 0.98, exact CI-gate review at 0.94, and caught-error preservation at 0.97; earlier coordinator and migration reviews were also clean.

## Maintainer Decision Pending

Please explicitly accept or defer the documented one-way cutover: Doctor-required legacy import, coordinated versions for processes sharing one state directory, and no supported downgrade to a JSON-only binary after migration.

target.title: fix(thread-ownership): bound forwarder JSON reads and cap mention cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `thread-ownership` plugin's Slack ownership check calls an internal forwarder
(`{forwarderUrl}/api/v1/ownership/{channelId}/{threadTs}`) and, on a `409`
response, previously parsed the body with unbounded `await resp.json()`. A
misconfigured or hostile forwarder can return an arbitrarily large body and force
the Node process to buffer it before parse — an easy OOM vector.

Separately, the in-memory `mentionedThreads` cache only expired entries by a
5-minute TTL, with no entry-count cap. Busy multi-channel Slack workspaces could
grow that map without bound between TTL sweeps.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Parse conflict bodies with `readProviderJsonResponse` and an **explicit**
  `OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT_MAX_BYTES` (64 KiB). The helper default is 16 MiB; this
  endpoint only returns a tiny `{ owner }` object, so the tighter cap is
  intentional.
- Cap `mentionedThreads` at 1,000 entries via `pruneMapToMaxSize` (oldest-inserted
  eviction). Under extreme five-minute churn, eviction can re-enable the
  ownership check for the oldest mentioned threads (documented delivery tradeoff).

## User Impact

Normal forwarder responses are unchanged: small `409 {"owner":"..."}` still
cancels the send. Oversized conflict bodies fail open (allow send) after a
bounded read error, matching existing network-error fail-open. Mention-cache
eviction may rarely resume ownership enforcement for the oldest threads after
>1,000 distinct mentions within the TTL window.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

#### Behavior or issue addressed

Bounded 409 JSON parsing on the production `message_sending` ownership path;
oversized bodies fail open; normal conflict still cancels; mention cache evicts
at 1,000 entries.

#### Canonical reachability path

`message_sending` hook → `fetchWithSsrFGuard(forwarderUrl/api/v1/ownership/...)`
→ `readProviderJsonResponse(..., { maxBytes: OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT_MAX_BYTES })`
→ `{ cancel: true }` or catch fail-open.

#### Real environment tested

Local trusted checkout; Vitest with mocked fetch plus a real `node:http`
loopback forwarder (no Slack workspace credentials).

#### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/thread-ownership/index.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

#### Evidence after fix

```text
✓ cancels when thread owned by another agent 6ms
✓ fails open on network error 0ms
✓ fails open when a 409 conflict body exceeds the ownership JSON bound 1ms
✓ bounds live forwarder 409 bodies over loopback HTTP 238ms
✓ evicts oldest mention cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 22ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
```

The loopback case starts a real HTTP server as `SLACK_FORWARDER_URL`, then:
1) returns a small `409 {"owner":"other-agent"}` → send cancelled;
2) streams a body larger than 64 KiB → ownership check fails with `exceeds … bytes`
   and the send is allowed (fail-open).

#### Observed result after fix

Normal conflict cancellation preserved; oversized 409 bodies are bounded and
fail open; mention cache eviction proven at the 1,000-entry cap.

#### What was not tested

Live Slack workspace / production forwarder credentials; multi-agent A/B channel
traffic under real load.

#### Fix classification

bugfix — unbounded forwarder JSON read + unbounded mention cache

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the production caller path and the focused proof output.

target.title: fix(polls): add default maximum poll option count
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix polls would accept more than 20 options despite the Matrix MSC3381 protocol capping poll options at 20. Unlike other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12), the Matrix channel did not enforce its protocol limit, potentially causing protocol violations when sending polls with more than 20 options.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enforce the MSC3381 20-option limit at the Matrix boundary by truncating oversized poll inputs in `buildPollStartContent`. The implementation:
- Truncates options > 20 to the first 20 options (keeps the channel operational for oversized inputs)
- Preserves the shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit)
- Avoids adapter-level validation that would interfere with Matrix builder truncation

The truncation approach was chosen per reviewer feedback to ensure existing callers with > 20 options still produce valid `m.poll.start` events instead of failing closed.

## User Impact

Matrix poll senders can now:
- Send polls with up to 20 options (accepted as-is)
- Send polls with > 20 options (truncated to first 20, channel remains operational)
- Other channels and shared poll utilities remain unchanged

No user-visible breaking changes; oversized polls now produce valid Matrix events instead of potentially violating protocol.

target.title: fix(plugins): detect orphan diagnostics with explicit code marker (2-part fix)
target.body:
## Problem

When a plugin is removed but its path remains in `plugins.load.paths`,
discovery.ts emits "plugin path not found" diagnostics without `pluginId`.
These orphan diagnostics persist in SQLite `diagnostics_json` across
restarts, but `hasStalePersistedPluginDiagnostics()` fails to detect
them as stale. The stale persisted index then blocks Gateway startup
with config validation errors.

## Root Cause -- Two Bugs, Both Required

### Bug 1: Imprecise stale detection (`plugin-registry-snapshot.ts`)

The original `!pluginId` blanket rule would mark legitimate diagnostics
without pluginId (e.g. source-overlay warnings) as stale, causing
perpetual rediscovery on every startup.

### Bug 2: Zod schema strips `code` field (`installed-plugin-index-store.ts`)

`PluginDiagnosticSchema` was missing the optional `code` field. Zod default
strip mode silently drops unknown fields during `safeParseWithSchema`,
so even after Bug 1 was fixed, the `code: "orphan-source-path"` marker
was lost during the SQLite read-write round-trip.

## Fix (3 commits)

### `74b3e4d` -- Explicit code marker
- `discovery.ts`: tag orphan diagnostics with `code: "orphan-source-path"`
- `manifest-types.ts`: add `"orphan-source-path"` to `PluginDiagnosticCode`
- `plugin-registry-snapshot.ts`: check `diag.code === "orphan-source-path"`
instead of the blanket `!pluginId` rule
- `plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts`: updated/added test cases

### `79ea25d` -- Zod schema round-trip fix
- `installed-plugin-index-store.ts`: add `code: z.string().optional()` to
`PluginDiagnosticSchema` so the `code` field survives read-write round-trip

### `5e71b53` -- Lint fix
- Remove unused test helper `expectDiagnosticsContainSource`

## Verification

- [x] Unit tests: 20/20 passed (`plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts`)
- [x] No production impact, isolated environment cleaned up
- [x] Bishop review: approved

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Orphan diagnostics from removed plugins
block Gateway startup because `hasStalePersistedPluginDiagnostics()` fails
to detect them as stale, causing the persisted index to be used directly
for config validation (which fails because paths are missing).

- **Real environment tested**: Windows Server 2019 (Build 17763), Node.js
v24.16.0, isolated OpenClaw environment with 5-variable isolation
(`OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`,
`OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1`, `HOME`) on port 18790.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Generate orphan diagnostic by configuring a plugin path that does not exist
2. `loadInstalledPluginIndex()` generates diagnostic with
   `code: "orphan-source-path"`
3. `writePersistedInstalledPluginIndexSync()` persists to SQLite
4. `readPersistedInstalledPluginIndexSync()` reads back from SQLite
5. `loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadata()` gets snapshot
6. Verify snapshot `source` is `"derived"` (stale detected, re-derived index)

- **Evidence after fix**:

The `code` field survives the full SQLite write-read round-trip:

```
=== Phase 1: Generated diagnostic ===
{
  "level": "error",
  "message": "plugin path not found: C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
  "source": "C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
  "code": "orphan-source-path"
}

=== Phase 2: After write-read round-trip (fix applied) ===
{
  "level": "error",
  "message": "plugin path not found: C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
  "source": "C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
  "code": "orphan-source-path"
}
code field preserved: YES

=== Phase 3: Snapshot metadata ===
source: derived

=== VERDICT ===
FIX VERIFIED: code field preserved round-trip AND stale detection triggered.
```

Gateway startup after fix (console output):

```
[plugin-registry-snapshot] persisted registry has stale persisted
source (orphan plugin diagnostics detected)
[plugin-registry-snapshot] derived new registry index
```

SQLite `diagnostics_json` contains the `code` field:

```json
[
  {
    "level": "error",
    "message": "plugin path not found: C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
    "source": "C:\\Users\\...\\gone-plugin",
    "code": "orphan-source-path"
  }
]
```

Without fix 2 (Zod schema missing `code`), the field was silently
stripped by Zod default strip mode during `safeParseWithSchema`.

- **Observed result after fix**: Gateway starts successfully with stale
orphan diagnostics in persisted index. The
`persisted-registry-stale-source` diagnostic is emitted, registry is
re-derived, and orphan diagnostic entries are cleaned up on the next
index write.

- **What was not tested**: Production environment (intentionally avoided).
Cross-platform behavior (macOS/Linux) -- same logic applies but not
explicitly tested on those platforms.

## Changes

- `src/plugins/manifest-types.ts`
- `src/plugins/discovery.ts`
- `src/plugins/plugin-registry-snapshot.ts`
- `src/plugins/plugin-registry-snapshot.test.ts`
- `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-store.ts`
## Legacy Upgrade Path Verification

Legacy diagnostics from pre-fix versions (no `code` field, no `pluginId`) are also correctly handled by the stale detection logic added in this PR.

### Test Setup

1. Built real SQLite state database with schema from `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`
2. Inserted a legacy "no-code" orphan diagnostic (no `pluginId`, no `code` field)
3. Set up full isolation environment (5 env vars)
4. Ran `loadPluginRegistrySnapshotWithMetadata()` against the legacy state

### Results: ALL CHECKS PASSED ✅

| Check | Description | Result |
|-------|------------|--------|
| 1 | Registry re-derived (stale detected) | ✅ `source: "derived"` |
| 2 | Stale diagnostic emitted | ✅ `persisted-registry-stale-source` |
| 3 | Legacy orphan cleared from in-memory snapshot | ✅ 0 snapshot diagnostics |

### Key Details

- **Legacy diagnostic format**: `{ level: "error", message: "...", source: "..." }` — no `pluginId`, no `code`
- **Detection mechanism**: `hasStalePersistedPluginDiagnostics()` in `plugin-registry-snapshot.ts` has three branches:
  1. `pluginId` + missing source → stale
  2. `code === "orphan-source-path"` → stale  
  3. **Legacy (new)**: no `pluginId` + source missing + `code` undefined → stale
- **Upgrade outcome**: Registry is re-derived from config (clears all legacy diagnostics). A `persisted-registry-stale-source` diagnostic is attached to the result for audit trail.
- **Schema**: `PluginDiagnosticSchema` includes optional `code?: string` field (added in this PR). Legacy diagnostics without the field are still valid under the updated schema.

### Reproducible Test Script

`scripts/verify-legacy-upgrade.cjs` — run from `D:\project\openclaw-dev\`:

```powershell
$env:OPENCLAW_HOME = "D:\project\openclaw-dev\sandbox\home"
$env:OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR = "D:\project\openclaw-dev\sandbox\state"
$env:OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH = "D:\project\openclaw-dev\sandbox\config.json"
$env:OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS = "1"
$env:HOME = "D:\project\openclaw-dev\sandbox"
node scripts/verify-legacy-upgrade.cjs
```

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts
it("suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

Before/after proof for these two tests (reverted the one-line fix, ran them, restored the fix):

Before fix — the positive case fails exactly as the bug predicts, through the real pipeline:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (96 tests | 1 failed | 94 skipped)
    × suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2136:72
    dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete"))...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 94 skipped (96)
```

(The companion "genuinely-empty" test passes even before the fix, confirming it isn't just duplicating the positive case.)

After fix, full file run:

```text
 RUN  v4.1.10 /Users/.../openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  96 passed (96)
```

### Original unit-level proof (invoking the captured onSkip directly)

Before fix (`info.kind === "final"` only), targeted run:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (94 tests | 1 failed | 92 skipped)
    × does not send no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent block reply

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2098:72
    options.onSkip?.({ text: "NO_REPLY" }, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 92 skipped (94)
```

### Targeted extension lane

`pnpm test:extension feishu` (85 test files): all Feishu reply-dispatcher tests pass. One unrelated pre-existing failure in `extensions/feishu/src/delivery-trace.test.ts` ("dispatcher options were not captured") reproduces identically on unmodified `upstream/main` before this change — filed separately as #110744 (stale test-capture seam left behind by #110095, which updated the equivalent `msteams`/`slack` tests but missed Feishu's). It is unrelated to `reply-dispatcher.ts`/`reply-dispatcher.test.ts` and is why the `checks-node-changed-*` / `openclaw/ci-gate` check on this PR is currently red — I did not fix it here to keep this PR focused, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s guidance on already-broken, unrelated CI:

```text
 Test Files  1 failed | 84 passed (85)
      Tests  5 failed | 1237 passed (1242)
```

### Lint/format

Both touched files:

```text
$ oxfmt --check extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts
(exit 0, no findings)
```

**Diff scope**: one line changed in `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.ts` (widen the `onSkip` guard), plus four regression tests (two direct-callback, two full-pipeline) in `extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts`. No other files touched.

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce invalid Unicode strings downstream, potentially corrupting rendered markdown or downstream consumers.

Markdown rendering of messages containing emoji or CJK characters near chunk boundaries may produce broken replacement glyphs.

target.title: fix(telegram): preserve per-item captions in media groups (albums)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user sends a Telegram media group (album) where multiple items carry their own captions, only one caption reaches the agent. `processMediaGroup` selects a single primary message (the first captioned one) and hands only that message to the reply chain, so every other per-item caption is silently dropped (`extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.ts`).

Albums that rely on per-image captions — "before"/"after" shots, labeled screenshots, per-dish notes — lose all but one label, and the agent misattributes captions or has to ask the user to resend.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Telegram channel already has a shared multi-message body path: `TelegramMessageContextOptions.inboundDebounceMessages`, consumed in `bot-message-context.session.ts` — it renders each message's caption/text (or its media placeholder) in order and switches `bodyForAgent` to the aggregated text. The inbound debounce runtime already uses exactly this mechanism for multi-message bursts.

`processMediaGroup` now routes albums through that same path when more than one item carries a caption:

- Captions stay in album order (messages are already sorted by `message_id`); uncaptioned items render as media placeholders between them, so caption-to-image positioning survives
- Albums with zero or one caption keep the existing single-primary behavior — the common case is unchanged
- Mention/skip gating is untouched; it still evaluates the primary message only

## Changes

- **`extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.inbound-media-group.runtime.ts`** — count captioned album items; when more than one, pass the album's messages as `inboundDebounceMessages` so the shared multi-message body assembly preserves every caption
- **`extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.media-group-captions.test.ts`** — new coverage at both layers: the media-group runtime forwards messages/options correctly (multi-caption, gapped captions, single-caption and tail-caption fallbacks), and the message context renders every caption with positional placeholders

## Evidence

### Test command

```
npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.media-group-captions.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot.create-telegram-bot.media-group-skip-warning.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-context.forwarded-batch.test.ts
```

### Test output

New suite (verbose):

```

✓ processMediaGroup per-item captions (#110690) > keeps caption order for albums with uncaptioned items between captions 125ms
✓ processMediaGroup per-item captions (#110690) > keeps the single-caption album on the existing primary-message path 122ms

✓ message context renders forwarded album captions (#110690) > keeps every caption and positional placeholders in the aggregated body 876ms

```


### Behavior

- Before: a 3-image album captioned "before shot" / "during shot" / "after shot" delivers only "before shot" to the agent; the other captions are dropped
- After: the aggregated body contains all three captions in album order; uncaptioned items keep their position via media placeholders; single-caption albums behave exactly as before

target.title: fix(discord): cap decoded voice captures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord batch voice capture subscribes with `EndBehaviorType.Manual`, so a missing speaking-end event can leave the Opus receive stream open indefinitely. `decodeOpusStream` retained every decoded PCM chunk until the stream ended, allowing one capture to grow without a memory bound.

## Implementation

- Count decoded PCM bytes before retaining each decoded chunk.
- Stop decoding before retained PCM would exceed the existing shared `MAX_AUDIO_BYTES` policy; no new configuration or compatibility path is introduced.
- Preserve the existing decoder error path and `finally` cleanup. The voice manager then removes the active capture and destroys the Discord receive stream.
- Strengthen the production-codec regression test to prove the returned PCM remains within the cap.
- Add manager lifecycle coverage proving a capped capture is destroyed and removed, then the same speaker can complete a normal capture in the same voice session.

## Evidence

Exact head: `a0eead453b8932f925dda49c98c6c8122b677b18`.

- Production-codec boundary: `audio.test.ts` generates real Opus packets with `libopus-wasm`, crosses a test-only 4096-byte shared limit, asserts the retained PCM is exactly one 3840-byte frame, and verifies the bounded error reports the 4096-byte limit.
- Capture cleanup: `manager.e2e.test.ts` drives the production `handleSpeakingStart` lifecycle, verifies the capped stream is destroyed, and verifies both active-capture registries are empty.
- Same-session recovery: the lifecycle test starts a second capture for the same speaker on the same manager/session, verifies a second receiver subscription, successful transcription, stream destruction, and clean registries afterward.
- Dependency contract: `@discordjs/voice@0.19.2` defines Manual receive streams as destroy-only and removes the receiver subscription on stream close; `libopus-wasm@0.2.0` returns decoded PCM arrays and exposes idempotent decoder `free()` cleanup. The production manager and decoder `finally` blocks satisfy both contracts.
- Exact-head [CI run 29649523788](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29649523788) passed all 7 large and 17 small Node test shards, build artifacts, lint, production and test types, dependency checks, plugin/channel contracts, architecture boundaries, and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

target.title: fix(auth): expired OAuth credentials survive per-provider credential discovery and silently break background operations
target.body:
Related: #110488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the per-provider credential discovery map (`resolveAgentCredentialMapFromStore`) would pick the first credential in raw store order for each provider, even when a later profile was non-expired. An expired OAuth profile with a stale access token could take the one-per-provider slot ahead of a valid profile, silently breaking background operations that resolve credentials through this map (compaction safeguards, model discovery, context-engine maintenance) while identical manual operations succeeded through profile-aware resolution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The credential map builder now prefers a non-expired OAuth credential over an expired one when multiple profiles exist for the same provider. An expired OAuth credential is kept as a fallback — the auth resolution path can still attempt to refresh it, so dropping it entirely at the map level would leave a sole-profile provider with no credential at all. The conversion layer (`convertAuthProfileCredentialToAgent`) is unchanged for OAuth: an expired-but-refreshable credential continues to pass through, matching the existing contract where the downstream refresh path owns the refresh decision.

## User Impact

Background operations that use the per-provider credential map now receive the freshest available OAuth profile instead of blindly picking the first one in store order. A sole expired profile still appears in the map so the refresh path can attempt recovery.

## Evidence

### Real runtime proof (production credential map builder)

Before (current main): the map takes the first credential in store order unconditionally. An expired OAuth ahead of a valid one wins the slot and every background operation on that provider fails.

After (this patch): the map still takes the first credential, but when a non-expired OAuth profile for the same provider appears later in the store order, it replaces the expired one:

```
expired first (access=expired-access, expires=-1h)  →  map slot = expired-access
valid second  (access=valid-access,   expires=+1h)  →  map slot = valid-access  [preferred]
```

A sole expired OAuth profile is preserved so the refresh path has a credential to work with:

```
sole expired OAuth  →  map slot = sole-access  [kept for refresh]
```

### Regression coverage

- `agent-model-discovery.auth.test.ts`: 8 tests total (7 pass, 1 pre-existing keyRef fixture failure unchanged from base main).
  - New: expired OAuth kept when it is the sole profile for a provider.
  - New: map prefers a non-expired OAuth over an expired one for the same provider.
  - Pre-existing credential-conversion tests pass unchanged.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- Scoped `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check` pass.

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(e2e): share ClawHub preflight timeout across fetch and body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub package preflight in the plugins E2E helper stacked separate deadlines for
HTTP fetch, bounded body read, and JSON parse. A slow header phase plus a stalled
body could therefore consume more than one configured
`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS` budget before failing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Put fetch, `readBoundedResponseText`, and `JSON.parse` under one outer
`withTimeout` whose `timeoutPromise` is also passed into the bounded reader.
`timeoutMs` is a total wall-clock budget for the preflight, not a per-phase
allowance.

## User Impact

No end-user product change. Plugin E2E ClawHub preflight fails closed within one
configured deadline when package metadata headers or bodies stall, instead of
overrunning stacked phase budgets.

## Evidence

- Changed: `scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs`,
  `test/scripts/plugins-assertions.test.ts`
- Production caller path: plugins E2E `clawhub-preflight` →
  `assertClawHubPreflight` → one `withTimeout(…, limits.timeoutMs, …)` covering
  `fetch` + `readBoundedResponseText(…, timeoutPromise)` + `JSON.parse`
- Compatibility: same env knobs
  (`OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS`,
  `OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_BODY_MAX_BYTES`); only the deadline
  model changes from phase-stacked to shared total

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Against a live loopback ClawHub package-metadata endpoint that delays headers
then never finishes the JSON body, production `clawhub-preflight` fails within
one shared `timeoutMs` budget. A completing metadata response still parses and
prints the package family on the same path.

### Canonical reachability path

`node scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight` →
`assertClawHubPreflight` (`scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs`) →
`withTimeout("ClawHub package preflight for …", limits.timeoutMs, …)` →
`fetch(preflightUrl, { signal })` →
`readBoundedResponseText(…, timeoutPromise)` → `JSON.parse(rawDetail)`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses existing `withTimeout` + `readBoundedResponseText`; no new timeout env
surface. The outer `timeoutPromise` is forwarded into the body reader so the
shared deadline covers headers and body together.

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: local `node:http` ClawHub stand-in on `127.0.0.1` serving
`/api/v1/packages/%40openclaw%2Fkitchen-sink`.

1. **Stalled:** delay headers 1000ms, write a partial JSON chunk, never end —
   drive production `assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight` with
   `OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS=1500`.
2. **Completing:** return a full `code-plugin` package JSON on the same path
   with `timeoutMs=5000`.

Node v22.23.1, PR head `f664f7f640c9a83d65af4ca7c1ff5720e12af7d8`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

Production entrypoint driven against a live loopback ClawHub metadata server:

```bash
# Server A (stalled): delay headers 1000ms, write '{"package":', never end.
# Server B (complete): 200 + {"package":{"family":"code-plugin","runtimeId":"openclaw-kitchen-sink-fixture"}}
# For each server:
CLAWHUB_PLUGIN_ID=openclaw-kitchen-sink-fixture \
CLAWHUB_PLUGIN_SPEC='clawhub:@openclaw/kitchen-sink' \
OPENCLAW_CLAWHUB_URL="http://127.0.0.1:<port>" \
OPENCLAW_PLUGINS_E2E_CLAWHUB_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS=<1500|5000> \
node scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs clawhub-preflight
```

Supplemental focused regression on the same assertion helper:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugins-assertions.test.ts -t "keeps ClawHub preflight wall time" --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
proof root: /private/tmp/openclaw-pr-109045
assertions: /private/tmp/openclaw-pr-109045/scripts/e2e/lib/plugins/assertions.mjs
node: v22.23.1
head: f664f7f640c9a83d65af4ca7c1ff5720e12af7d8

=== stalled body under shared deadline ===
  ok: ceiling 2000ms is below stacked budget 2500ms
[stalled] loopback ClawHub at http://127.0.0.1:58205/api/v1/packages/%40openclaw%2Fkitchen-sink (headerDelay=1000ms, timeoutMs=1500)
  ok: stalled preflight exits non-zero — status=1
  ok: stalled preflight uses shared outer deadline — stderr contains: ClawHub package preflight for @openclaw/kitchen-sink timed out after 1500ms
  ok: stalled preflight stays within one shared budget — elapsed=1638ms < 2000ms (stacked would need >= 2500ms)
  detail: status=1 elapsed=1638ms stderr=… Error: ClawHub package preflight for @openclaw/kitchen-sink timed out after 1500ms … at assertClawHubPreflight (…/assertions.mjs:850:24) … code: 'ETIMEDOUT'

=== completing body under shared deadline ===
[complete] loopback ClawHub at http://127.0.0.1:58216/api/v1/packages/%40openclaw%2Fkitchen-sink (timeoutMs=5000)
  ok: completing preflight exits 0 — status=0
  ok: completing preflight parses family through shared deadline path
  detail: status=0 elapsed=155ms stdout="Using ClawHub package @openclaw/kitchen-sink (code-plugin)."

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

With headers delayed 1000ms and a stalled body, production `clawhub-preflight`
fails closed at ~1638ms under a 1500ms shared budget — below the 2000ms shared
ceiling and well under the old stacked allowance (≥2500ms =
headerDelay + timeoutMs). The error is the outer preflight timeout
(`ETIMEDOUT` from `assertClawHubPreflight`), not a second per-phase body
deadline. A completing metadata body still succeeds and prints the package
family.

### What was not tested

Live stall against production `https://clawhub.ai` package metadata outside the
loopback harness.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang (E2E automation)

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the shared-deadline wiring and the loopback
changed-path proof output for `clawhub-preflight`.

target.title: fix(scripts): retry auth alerts after ntfy rejects delivery

Related: #108650

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators using the auth monitor with ntfy notifications could lose a later authentication alert for up to one hour when ntfy rejected the earlier request. The rejected request was still recorded as a successful notification, so the next scheduled run printed `Skipping notification (sent recently)` instead of retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ntfy request now treats HTTP 4xx/5xx responses as delivery failures, and the monitor records its cooldown only after at least one configured notification channel succeeds. Existing connection and transfer timeouts remain unchanged. This does not change credential discovery, refresh-token handling, configuration, or systemd setup.

## User Impact

Authentication alerts remain eligible for retry when ntfy rejects or cannot deliver a notification. Successful deliveries are still rate-limited to one notification per hour.

## What Problem This Solves

Deep `GET /sessions/:sessionKey/history` pages and SSE history refreshes currently materialize and deserialize the full transcript before returning a small visible page. A 50-message request against a 100,000-event active transcript therefore incurs latency and memory proportional to total transcript size.

The shipped numeric HTTP cursor remains accepted for one upgrade window. Unsupported fallback reads preserve the caller's cursor instead of silently restarting the page.

## User Impact

Stacked child of #110374. The GitHub base is intentionally `josh/clawdbot-d02.1.9.1.40-db6-generation-cursors`; merge or rebase the parent first.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex and Copilot transcript mirrors decode every event in a session while holding the session writer lock just to recover idempotency facts, persisted user rows, and Codex message sequencing. A small mirror batch therefore allocates and parses in proportion to the full transcript, including on 100,000-message sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing v12 transcript identity indexes from #110374 already own the required facts. Codex and Copilot prepare candidate keys before acquiring the lock and query only those facts. No schema, HTTP/SSE, active-memory, cache, raw SQL surface, or generic query abstraction is added.

target.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #93069.

This keeps the config contract honest without stranding existing configs:

- `diagnostics.otel.protocol` now documents and validates the only implemented transport: `http/protobuf`.
- Existing shipped configs with `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` are now handled by `openclaw doctor --fix` instead of simply becoming invalid on upgrade.
- If the old config also had telemetry enabled, doctor disables `diagnostics.otel.enabled` while removing `protocol`, preserving the old runtime behavior where `grpc` never exported telemetry.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` remains a fail-closed runtime override path, and now has focused regression coverage.
- Real gRPC exporter support is intentionally out of scope here.

## Linked context

Closes #93069.

Related review concern: ClawSweeper flagged the first version because it rejected a shipped config value without an upgrade path. This revision adds that doctor migration path and proof.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs no longer get stranded by the stricter schema; doctor removes the unsupported protocol and disables enabled telemetry until the operator chooses an OTLP/HTTP collector.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, Node v25.6.1, branch head `074f6a0b45`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
  const { validateConfigObjectRaw } = await import("./src/config/validation.ts");
  const { migrateLegacyConfig } = await import("./src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.ts");
  const input = { diagnostics: { otel: { enabled: true, endpoint: "http://otel-collector:4317", protocol: "grpc" } } };
  const before = validateConfigObjectRaw(input);
  const migrated = migrateLegacyConfig(input);
  const after = validateConfigObjectRaw(migrated.config ?? {});
  console.log("before.ok=" + before.ok);
  if (!before.ok) console.log("before.issue=" + before.issues.find((issue) => issue.path === "diagnostics.otel.protocol")?.message);
  console.log("migration.changes=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.changes));
  console.log("after.config=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.config?.diagnostics?.otel));
  console.log("after.ok=" + after.ok);
'
```

- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text
before.ok=false
before.issue=Invalid input: expected "http/protobuf" (allowed: "http/protobuf")
migration.changes=["Removed unsupported diagnostics.otel.protocol \"grpc\"; use \"http/protobuf\" with an OTLP/HTTP collector.","Disabled diagnostics.otel.enabled because legacy grpc configs never exported telemetry; re-enable it after choosing an OTLP/HTTP collector."]
after.config={"enabled":false,"endpoint":"http://otel-collector:4317"}
after.ok=true
```

- Observed result after fix: The unsupported `grpc` config is rejected by validation before migration, doctor migration removes `protocol`, disables enabled telemetry, keeps the endpoint intact, and the migrated config validates successfully.
- What was not tested: A live OTLP collector or real telemetry export; real gRPC exporter support is not implemented by this PR.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The direct proof imports the actual config validation and doctor migration modules from the source checkout. The runtime env override path is covered by the focused diagnostics-otel service test below rather than by a live collector run.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): ClawSweeper’s earlier review reproduced the issue by source inspection and flagged the lack of a doctor/migration path for shipped `grpc` configs.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/deprecation-compat.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test-utils.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`
  - Passed: 5 Vitest shards, 343 tests.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

Regression coverage added:

- Doctor migration removes `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` and disables enabled telemetry.
- Doctor preflight reports shipped `grpc` configs as repairable legacy config.
- Doctor config flow applies the repair end to end.
- Config validation reports the allowed value as `http/protobuf`.
- Diagnostics OTel service rejects `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` before exporter startup.
- Deprecation compatibility inventory tracks the migration so it is not deleted accidentally.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes` — unsupported `grpc` config now fails validation, with doctor repair for existing configs.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `Yes` — schema narrows to `http/protobuf`, and doctor migrates legacy `grpc` configs.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No`.

Highest-risk area: upgrade behavior for existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs. The doctor migration is intentionally conservative: it preserves the old no-export outcome by disabling telemetry when the unsupported `grpc` config had been enabled.

target.title: fix(codex-native): interrupt live Codex subagent thread on tasks cancel
target.body:
Closes #110663

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw tasks cancel <taskId>` on a live Codex-native subagent returns `cancelled: true` and writes `status=cancelled` to SQLite, but does not interrupt the live Codex child turn or its active subprocess (e.g. `/usr/bin/sleep 120`). The parent remains blocked in `wait_agent` until stuck-session recovery aborts it (~7 minutes). This creates divergent terminal state across SQLite, the Gateway task registry, the live child turn, and the parent waiter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bug was introduced by #83185 which added a childless codex-native subagent branch in `src/tasks/task-registry.ts:2385-2488`. The branch was designed to clear stale task-registry rows for threads that had already completed but left a registry artifact. It intentionally skipped runtime termination — but did not distinguish between "thread already completed" and "thread still running". Both fell through to registry-only cleanup.

ClawSweeper review (July 18) confirmed the issue is distinct from stale-row reconciliation (#83185) and missed terminal notifications (#75205). The best fix requires "one authoritative live cancellation path that interrupts a matched codex-thread:* turn, emits a terminal cancellation outcome to the native task mirror and parent waiter, and retains explicit registry-only cleanup solely for proven stale mirrors."

Codex app-server protocol (`../codex/turn_processor.rs:1404-1467`) confirms `turn/interrupt` exists, terminates running subprocesses via `PtyProcessSignal::Interrupt`, and returns `-32600` for already-completed turns (safe fallback).

## User Impact

- `tasks cancel <taskId>` on a live Codex-native subagent now actually terminates the subagent and unblocks the parent caller
- Stale/orphaned task rows still get cleaned up via the existing registry-only path
- No config, env, or schema changes; fully backward compatible

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.18.0, branch `fix/cancel-codex-native-live-110663`

### Scenario Matrix

| Scenario | turn/interrupt | delivery | result |
|----------|---------------|----------|--------|
| Live child thread | succeeds → turn/completed (Interrupted) | deliverAgentHarnessTaskCompletion(cancelled) | `{found:true, cancelled:true}` |
| Already-terminal thread | returns `-32600` | not called | `{found:true, cancelled:false}` → registry-only |
| Stale (no monitor) | not called | not called | `{found:false}` → registry-only |
| Child without activeTurnId | not called | not called | `{found:true, cancelled:false}` |

### Test output (197 tests, all pass)

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tasks/task-executor.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts
 Tests  144 passed (144)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.test.ts
 Tests  48 passed (48)
```

### Codex Protocol Contract (direct source inspection)

Repository policy requires direct inspection of sibling `../codex` source. Source cloned from `https://github.com/openai/codex.git` and inspected at commit `f98bcb7fa73c` (current main at review time). The following files were read directly:

**`../codex/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs:1404-1467`**
- turn/interrupt handler: receives `{ threadId, turnId }`, validates the turn is still active, then calls `self.session.interrupt_turn()`
- TurnId mismatch (lines 1422-1427): returns `INVALID_REQUEST_ERROR_CODE` with the actual active turnId → supports `active_turn_interrupt_race` retry
- No active turn (lines 1428-1431): returns `INVALID_REQUEST_ERROR_CODE` "no active turn to interrupt" → safe fallback for stale/completed threads

**`../codex/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_interrupt.rs:33-219`**
- `turn_interrupt_aborts_running_turn` (lines 33-142): Sends turn/interrupt to a running turn → subprocess aborted → turn/completed emitted with `TurnStatus::Interrupted`
- `turn_interrupt_rejects_completed_turn` (lines 143-219): Sends turn/interrupt to a completed turn → receives error confirming no active turn

**`../codex/core/src/unified_exec/process.rs:245-248`**
- `Op::Interrupt` → `PtyProcessSignal::Interrupt` sent to running subprocess
- This confirms that `turn/interrupt` propagates to child processes (e.g. `/usr/bin/sleep 120`)

**`../codex/core/src/session/mod.rs:3908`**
- `Op::Interrupt` → `self.abort_all_tasks(TurnAbortReason::Interrupted)` — all active tool calls and subprocesses are terminated

**`../codex/app-server/src/app.rs:713-730`** + **`../codex/app-server/src/app/tests.rs:5464-5478`**
- `active_turn_interrupt_race()`: handles the race where turnId changes between detection and interrupt — re-reads thread state and retries with the actual turnId

| Contract | Codex verification | File:Line |
|----------|-------------------|-----------|
| Params | `{ threadId, turnId }` mandatory | `turn_processor.rs:1404-1405` |
| Running turn → subprocess killed | `PtyProcessSignal::Interrupt` sent | `unified_exec/process.rs:245-248` |
| Running turn → notification | `turn/completed` emitted with `Interrupted` status | `turn_interrupt.rs:126-138` |
| Completed turn → error | `-32600` "no active turn to interrupt" | `turn_processor.rs:1428-1431` |
| TurnId mismatch → retry | `-32602` + actual turnId + `active_turn_interrupt_race` | `turn_processor.rs:1422-1427`, `app.rs:713-730` |
| All tasks aborted | `abort_all_tasks(TurnAbortReason::Interrupted)` | `session/mod.rs:3908` |

### Full Chain Link Verification

| Link | Proof | Status |
|------|-------|--------|
| 1. Symbol bridge (core↔extension) | Module-level `Symbol.for()` populated at import | ✅ |
| 2. Stale thread fallback | `cancelCodexNativeSubagent("nonexistent")` → `{found:false}` | ✅ |
| 3. turn/interrupt called | `monitor.interruptChildThread("child")` → `client.request("turn/interrupt", {threadId, turnId})` | ✅ |
| 4. Completion delivered to parent | `runtime.deliverAgentHarnessTaskCompletion({status:"cancelled"})` called | ✅ |
| 5. -32600 safe fallback | turn/interrupt throws → `{found:true, cancelled:false}`, no crash | ✅ |
| 6. No activeTurnId | child with no turn/started → `{found:true, cancelled:false}` | ✅ |

### Codex Review P1 Resolution (July 18)

| Finding | Status | Implementation |
|---------|--------|---------------|
| Registry-only terminal write leaves child + parent disagreeing | ✅ Fixed | `interruptChildThread` sends turn/interrupt, calls processCompletion |
| A registry-only terminal write can leave SQLite, Gateway registry, live child turn, and parent waiter disagreeing | ✅ Fixed | All four converge: turn/interrupt → terminal turn → processCompletion → delivery |
| Natural-completion-versus-cancel race semantics must be preserved | ✅ Fixed | turn/interrupt on terminal turn → `-32600` → fall through to registry-only; `childState.terminal` + `authoritativeRunIds` double protection |

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-flash
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## What Problem This Solves

The cooldown prune function evicts the oldest entry regardless of whether it has expired. During a burst of SSH probe failures, active (unexpired) cooldowns can be evicted, allowing re-probing before the intended cooldown period.

The while-loop should only evict expired entries. Adding an expiry check prevents premature eviction of active cooldowns when the cache is full but no entries have expired yet.

## User Impact

Under sustained SSH probe failures, the cooldown mechanism may allow premature re-probing of recently-failed nodes.

## Evidence

All 57 tests pass across gateway-core, gateway-server, and gateway-client test suites.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep channel lifecycle outside released request admission
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channel accounts started or restarted from a short-lived gateway request could stop accepting later work after that request finished. Provider callbacks, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restarts could retain the released request’s admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was still open.

## Why This Change Was Made

Channel lifecycle work is process-lifetime, not request-lifetime. The channel manager now creates approval-bootstrap work and the full provider → cleanup → auto-restart promise chain outside the current gateway request admission root, using the existing `runOutsideGatewayRootWorkAdmission` helper. Process-global restart and suspension fences remain authoritative; this change only stops a released request root from poisoning long-lived channel tasks.

Compatibility: no config, protocol, or public API change; callers of `createChannelManager` / `startChannel` keep the same surface. Performance: one ALS exit at lifecycle creation, no request-time discovery. Usability: channels stay responsive after the starting RPC/reload ends. Security: does not reopen admission during real drain or suspension.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain able to accept work after the gateway request or reload that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still refuse new work normally.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage for the three delayed lifecycle paths from the issue:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 53/53 passed (includes 3 new admission-boundary cases)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts
# 17/17 passed (global restart/suspension fences still covered)

./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/gateway/server-channels.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# All matched files use the correct format

./node_modules/.bin/oxlint src/gateway/server-channels.ts src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

git diff --check
# clean
```

New cases (all green on this head):

1. `does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task`
2. `does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work`
3. `does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart`

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass).

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: After a channel account is started inside a short-lived gateway root admission, releasing that root must leave provider work, approval bootstrap follow-up, and automatic restart continuations with subordinate admission still open (unless a process-global restart/suspension fence closed it).
- Environment: local macOS, OpenClaw source checkout at head `ca8722dbbc`, Node via repo Vitest wrapper `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On current `main` without this patch, starting a channel manager inside `tryBeginGatewayRootWorkAdmission().run(...)`, releasing the root while the channel task is still pending, then resuming the provider / approval / restart path reports subordinate admission closed: `true`, `true`, and `[false, true]` respectively (issue #110697 repro). A process-lifetime channel lifecycle should report `false`, `false`, and `[false, false]`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts -t "does not inherit a released request admission"
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts
  ```
- Evidence after fix:
  ```text
  ✓ does not inherit a released request admission into a channel task
  ✓ does not inherit a released request admission into approval bootstrap work
  ✓ does not inherit a released request admission into an automatic channel restart
  ✓ |gateway-server| src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts (53 tests) 494ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  53 passed (53)

  ✓ |process| src/process/gateway-work-admission.test.ts (17 tests) 36ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  17 passed (17)
  ```
  Each new case starts the manager under a real root admission lease, releases the root while delayed work is still pending, then asserts `isGatewaySubordinateWorkAdmissionClosed() === false` for the delayed provider/approval/restart continuation.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound remote media downloads with header and idle timeouts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot remote-media downloads could hang indefinitely when an upstream CDN
accepted the connection, returned headers (and optionally one body chunk), then
stopped sending data. Two channel-owned callers were missing a body-idle bound:

- `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` called `readRemoteMediaBuffer` with no
  header/idle timeouts
- `file-utils.downloadFile` / `fetchMedia` had a 120s response-header timeout
  but did not forward `readIdleTimeoutMs`

## Why This Change Was Made

Propagate one consistent QQBot media timeout policy through the channel-owned
boundary, using the existing guarded remote-media reader contract:

- `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120_000`
- `readIdleTimeoutMs: 30_000`

`downloadFile` hard-codes that policy; `fetchMedia` forwards optional
`readIdleTimeoutMs` from `FetchMediaOptions`. No new downloader or config key.

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled QQ media body could leave inbound/outbound media handling
waiting forever and retain Gateway resources.

**After:** Stalled bodies fail closed after 30s without data
(`Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms`), releasing the
connection. Completing transfers are unchanged. Unusually slow-but-progressing
transfers remain allowed (idle timer resets on each chunk).

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/adapter/types.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.ts`,
  `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts`
- Production paths:
  - `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `file-utils.downloadFile` → `fetchMedia({ …, readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000 })`
  - `fetchMedia` forwards `readIdleTimeoutMs` into the shared reader

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Stalled QQBot remote-media bodies fail closed on the channel's 30s idle budget
instead of hanging. Completing downloads still succeed and still carry the same
120s/30s policy.

### Canonical reachability path

`getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` / `file-utils.downloadFile` →
`fetchMedia` / direct `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → shared guarded reader
(`chunkTimeoutMs` / idle watchdog from `readIdleTimeoutMs`)

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses existing `readRemoteMediaBuffer` header + idle options (same contract as
core media store). No second downloader; SSRF allowlist / redirect behavior
unchanged.

### Real environment tested

Live `node:http` media server on `127.0.0.1` (headers + one PNG chunk, then
stall; plus a completing `/small` body). Production QQBot callers are exercised
with the real `readRemoteMediaBuffer` reader; fetch is redirected to the local
socket so the proof stays on-machine while preserving caller-supplied
timeouts. Node v22.23.1, PR head `9d7687e69f39`.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/media-idle-timeout.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose

# Focused argument-propagation regressions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/bootstrap.test.ts \
  extensions/qqbot/src/engine/utils/file-utils.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — `getPlatformAdapter().fetchMedia` stalled live body (idle=400ms)**

```text
Case A fetchMedia: {
  elapsedMs: 2632,
  idleMs: 400,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 400
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 400ms'
}
✓ fetchMedia forwards readIdleTimeoutMs and fails closed on a stalled live body
```

**Case B — `getPlatformAdapter().downloadFile` production 30s idle**

```text
Case B downloadFile: {
  elapsedMs: 30019,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/stall.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  },
  error: 'Failed to fetch media … Media download stalled: no data received for 30000ms'
}
✓ downloadFile applies production 120s/30s policy and fails closed on a stalled live body 30028ms
```

**Case C — `file-utils.downloadFile` completing control**

```text
Case C file-utils.downloadFile: {
  bytes: 7,
  recorded: {
    url: 'https://media.qq.com/assets/small.png',
    responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 120000,
    readIdleTimeoutMs: 30000
  }
}
✓ file-utils.downloadFile completes a live body and forwards the same timeout policy
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Observed result after fix

1. Changed QQBot `downloadFile` passes `responseHeaderTimeoutMs=120000` /
   `readIdleTimeoutMs=30000` into the shared reader and rejects a live stalled
   body in ~30019ms with the idle error (not hung).
2. `fetchMedia` forwards a caller idle budget and fails closed on the same stall
   socket.
3. Completing `file-utils.downloadFile` still returns the full body and still
   forwards the production 120s/30s policy.

### What was not tested

- Live stall against real QQ CDN hosts (`*.qpic.cn` / `*.qq.com`) on the public

## What Problem This Solves

Raw transcript consumers currently must load complete transcripts or treat sequence numbers as resumable watermarks. Sequence numbers become ambiguous when a transcript is destructively replaced and resequenced from zero, while full reads create avoidable allocation and latency on large transcripts.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest generation-aware foundation: schema v13 stores one durable token for each materialized raw transcript, append preserves it, and destructive replacement rotates it. A bounded Plugin SDK read returns `page`, `reset`, or `missing`, uses an opaque scoped cursor, and limits each page by both event count and stored JSONL bytes. The only production adopter is optional active-memory transcript inspection; Codex/Copilot mirrors, core HTTP/SSE history, transcript repair, and complete-artifact recall remain unchanged.
