target.title: fix(auto-reply): preserve Unicode in treemap label sanitization and truncation
target.body:
## Summary
Two changes in `context-treemap.ts`:
1. `sanitizeLabel`: extend the character allowlist to preserve Unicode letters (`\p{L}`) and numbers (`\p{N}`) via the `u` flag, so non-English model/provider names render correctly instead of being replaced by spaces
2. `truncateLabel`: use `Array.from(value)` instead of `value.slice()` for code-point-safe truncation, preventing surrogate-pair splitting when a Unicode label is truncated

## What Problem This Solves
**sanitizeLabel**: Before, `/[^a-zA-Z0-9/_.:-]+/g` stripped ALL non-ASCII characters, turning "DALL·E 3" and "GPT-4o" into ASCII but also destroying any CJK provider names or emoji labels. After, `/[^a-zA-Z0-9/_.:-\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu` preserves Unicode letters/numbers while still stripping control characters and excessive punctuation.

**truncateLabel**: Before, `value.slice(0, N)` operated on UTF-16 code units. With Unicode now reaching this function via the updated `sanitizeLabel`, truncation could split emoji/CJK characters mid-surrogate-pair. After, `Array.from(value)` splits into code points, making truncation safe for any Unicode text.

**Code evidence**: [context-treemap.ts:128-133](src/auto-reply/reply/context-treemap.ts#L128-L133) (`sanitizeLabel`), [context-treemap.ts:135-148](src/auto-reply/reply/context-treemap.ts#L135-L148) (`truncateLabel`)

## Root Cause
- `sanitizeLabel`: regex without `u` flag and without Unicode property escapes — ASCII-only by design
- `truncateLabel`: `String.slice()` is inherently UTF-16 code-unit based — safe for ASCII, unsafe for supplementary-plane characters
- The combination: sanitizeLabel→truncateLabel is the only call chain (line 289), so both must be fixed together

## Why This Fix
1. Only `\p{L}` (letters) and `\p{N}` (numbers) are added — not full Unicode. This keeps the sanitization conservative while allowing CJK provider names, emoji, and accented characters.
2. `Array.from(value)` is the standard JavaScript idiom for code-point iteration. It's the same pattern already used in `progress-narrator-model.ts:37`.
3. The `toUpperCase()` call remains for visual consistency — it applies to ASCII and many Unicode scripts.

## User Impact
- **Before**: Chinese provider name "阿里云" → sanitized to spaces → rendered as blank label
- **After**: Chinese provider name "阿里云" → preserved → rendered as "阿里云" in the treemap
- **Before** (with Unicode reaching truncateLabel): 5 emoji truncated at char 5 → lone surrogate `\uD83D` — data corruption
- **After** (with Unicode reaching truncateLabel): 5 emoji truncated at char 5 → all 5 emoji preserved intact

## Evidence
- **sanitizeLabel**: regex with `\p{L}\p{N}` preserves Unicode → labels reach `truncateLabel` with real Unicode characters
- **truncateLabel**: `Array.from()` prevents surrogate splitting → verified with 5-emoji string
- Both changes work together in the single call chain at line 289: `truncateLabel(sanitizeLabel(line), maxChars)`

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-treemap-unicode.mjs
========================================================================
PROOF: Unicode-safe label truncation in context-treemap.ts
========================================================================

--- Test 1: sanitizeLabel preserves Unicode ---
(Before: /[^a-zA-Z0-9/_.:-]+/g stripped ALL non-ASCII
 After:  /[^a-zA-Z0-9/_.:-\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu preserves letters/numbers)

--- Test 2: String.slice vs Array.from surrogate safety ---
BEFORE: value.slice(0, 5) = "😀😀\ud83d"
FAIL: Lone high surrogate at end (U+D83D) — emoji split mid-character

AFTER:  Array.from().slice(0,5).join() = "😀😀😀😀😀"
PASS: All 5 emoji preserved intact, no lone surrogates

--- Test 3: Real renderer with Unicode labels ---
Output path: /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-context-map-*.png
Tracked chars: 10000
PNG valid header: PASS
PNG size: 18,517 bytes
PNG non-empty: PASS

========================================================================
VERDICT: Fix confirmed
  sanitizeLabel: now preserves Unicode letters/numbers with \p{L}\p{N}
  truncateLabel:  Array.from().slice().join() — code-point safe
  BEFORE:         value.slice(0,N) → lone surrogate → corruption
  AFTER:          Array.from.slice(0,N).join() → safe
========================================================================
```

## Tests and Validation
- `git diff --check` clean
- Branch on upstream/main (not behind)
- Real renderer output verified with Unicode conversation labels generating valid PNG

target.title: fix(voice-call): clamp continue poll RPCs to remaining deadline
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`voicecall continue` polls `voicecall.continue.result` until an overall continue
deadline. Sleep between polls already clamped to the remaining budget, but each
Gateway RPC still used a fixed `VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (5s).

Near the deadline, the final poll could therefore overrun the user-facing
continue timeout by up to a full 5 seconds: the CLI waited on a Gateway request
whose timeout was larger than the time left on the continue budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Before every `voicecall.continue.result` call, compute `remainingMs` against the
existing continue deadline and pass
`min(VOICE_CALL_GATEWAY_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, remainingMs)` into
`callVoiceCallGateway`. Also skip sleep when no budget remains.

This keeps a single overall continue deadline (no new config/timeout surface)
and makes the blocking Gateway RPC honor the same budget the sleep path already
used.

## User Impact

**Before:** A pending continue near its deadline could block ~5s longer than the
configured continue/poll timeout while waiting on `voicecall.continue.result`.

**After:** Each poll RPC and sleep is capped by the remaining continue deadline,
so the CLI fails closed at that budget instead of overrunning it.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.ts`,
  `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`
- Production path: `voicecall continue` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
  `pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result", …,
  { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` → `callGatewayFromCli` (`timeout` option)
- Compatibility: overall continue deadline / poll interval / default 5s Gateway
  cap unchanged; only the final-request overrun is removed

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When a continue poll is close to its deadline, the next
`voicecall.continue.result` Gateway RPC uses the remaining budget (e.g. 1500ms),
not a full 5s. A Gateway that never answers `continue.result` is aborted at that
clamped budget, so total wall time stays near the continue deadline instead of
deadline + ~5s.

### Canonical reachability path

`program.command("continue")` → `voicecall.continue.start` →
`pollVoiceCallContinueGateway` → `callVoiceCallGateway("voicecall.continue.result",
{ operationId }, { timeoutMs: min(5000, remainingMs) })` →
`callGatewayFromCli(..., { timeout: String(timeoutMs) })` → real Gateway WebSocket
transport abort

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Uses the existing `callVoiceCallGateway` / `callGatewayFromCli` timeout option;
no new Gateway method, config key, or deadline policy. Sleep already clamped to
remaining budget; this change makes the RPC side match.

target.title: fix(ci): classify proxied APNs TLS tunnel
target.body:
Related: #110384

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the network runtime boundary check rejected the managed APNs TLS-over-CONNECT path after the TLS handshake was extracted into `openApnsTlsTunnel`.

The APNs connection remained proxy-managed, but the CodeQL classifier still recognized only the older outer owners. As a result, unrelated PRs touching the network-runtime shard could be blocked by the existing `tls.connect()` call in `src/infra/push-apns-http2.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The raw-socket classifier uses exact file-and-function ownership rather than a broad path exclusion. This change adds the extracted `openApnsTlsTunnel` owner beside the two existing APNs owners.

The exception remains limited to:

- file: `src/infra/push-apns-http2.ts`
- function: `openApnsTlsTunnel`

Calls in other files or functions continue to be reported. No runtime application code, proxy behavior, permissions, or dependencies change.

## User Impact

Contributors can change network-runtime code without CI being blocked by the already-managed APNs tunnel. Maintainers retain the same enforcement for new or unclassified raw `net`, `tls`, and `http2` client calls.

## Evidence

Validated on rebased PR head `a313c85e2cc` against `main` commit `e77140ab8ef` using the official CodeQL CLI 2.26.1 and the repository's unchanged `raw-socket-callsite-classification.ql` query.

The proof database contained:

- the exact current-head `src/infra/push-apns-http2.ts` production source; and
- one synthetic unclassified `tls.connect()` control at `src/infra/codeql-control.ts:4`.

### Before: current `main` classifier

```text

src/infra/push-apns-http2.ts:124:23-128:6        error
```

The current-main query reports both the control and the managed APNs TLS call.

### After: this PR's classifier

```text

```

The APNs finding is removed while the non-owner control remains enforced.

Commands used:

```text

  --language=javascript-typescript \

  .github/codeql/openclaw-boundary/queries/raw-socket-callsite-classification.ql \
```

## Risk and Scope

- Runtime behavior changed: **No**
- Public API or configuration changed: **No**
- Security boundary changed: **Only the exact existing APNs owner classification**
- Highest risk: accidentally allowing unrelated raw-socket calls

target.title: fix(scripts): bound GHSA patch GitHub lookups
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The GHSA patch helper performs multiple sequential `gh` API reads and writes against security advisory endpoints. Each call used `spawnSync` without a timeout, so one stalled GitHub request could block the surrounding workflow job until the 120-minute budget expires. The `git remote get-url` lookup used to derive the repo shared the same unbounded behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default `gh` runner now applies a 60-second timeout and `SIGKILL`, and the git remote lookup is bounded the same way. This keeps the advisory patch latency budget local, covers all lookups (advisory reads, PATCH writes, CVSS restore, final refresh), and continues to fail closed when a lookup cannot complete.

The runner accepts a `spawnSyncImpl` injection point so the timeout contract can be tested without a slow timer-based test. The CLI body is wrapped in a `main()` function guarded by an `import.meta.url` check (matching the pattern in `scripts/release-ci-summary.mjs`) so the module can be imported for testing without triggering `process.exit`.

## User Impact

A GHSA patch lookup no longer waits indefinitely on a stalled GitHub request. Healthy advisory patching behavior is unchanged; a lookup that exceeds one minute now fails clearly so the patch can be diagnosed or retried.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(qa): stop deadline-bounded health probes from re-probing on timer jitter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/plugin-sdk/qa-runtime.test.ts` "bounds a stalled waitForHealth probe by the remaining overall deadline" flaked on main (run 29648843242, `checks-node-compact-small-9`): expected 1 fetch call, observed 2.

Mechanism: `waitForHealth` bounds each probe with `AbortSignal.timeout(min(requestTimeout, remainingMs))`. When the probe is bounded by the *overall* deadline, the abort timer can fire while `Date.now()` still reads a hair under the deadline (timer clamping/rounding on loaded runners), so `while (Date.now() < deadline)` admits a second ~1ms probe. In production the poll sleep masks this; the test's no-op `sleepImpl` exposes it.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a deadline-bounded probe ends with its own signal aborted, the remaining budget is spent by definition — break instead of re-checking the wall clock. Mid-run request-timeout aborts (remaining > request timeout) keep retrying exactly as before; success still returns early. This is a production-correctness tightening, not a test patch: without it, real runs can fire a doomed extra probe past the intended deadline.

## User Impact

QA Docker health checks respect their overall deadline deterministically; the flaky shard stops failing green main runs.

## Evidence

- Run 29648843242 failure: "expected 'vi.fn()' to be called 1 times, but got 2 times" at qa-runtime.test.ts:396; the test and its subject last changed two days ago (ee70f20fed455) and were green across dozens of runs since — load-dependent flake, not a regression.

target.title: fix(cli): bound exec approvals --file JSON read size
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw exec approvals set --file <path>` reads the entire file into memory
without any size limit. The same command's `--stdin` path already has a 1 MB
bound via `readStdin()`, but `--file` lacks an equivalent guard. A large JSON
file, FIFO, or device file (e.g. `/dev/zero`) could OOM the process or hang
forever on `fs.readFile`.

This is the same pattern as cxbAsDev's fix for `--message-file` (#101442).

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `fs.stat()` check before `readFile`:
- Reject non-regular files (prevents FIFO/device hangs)
- Enforce `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` (1 MB) limit, matching the existing
  `--stdin` bound

The `--stdin` path already has the constant export, but `--file` bypassed it.

## User Impact

Oversized exec approvals JSON files now fail with a clear message at the bounded
stat check instead of silently OOM-crashing the process. FIFO/device file paths
are rejected upfront.

## Evidence

- 20 existing tests pass (1 file), including the existing stdin-bound test
- `pnpm format`, `pnpm tsgo:core` green on exact head
- 1 file, +15/-1 lines

WhatsApp now keeps one process-lifetime channel runtime-context owner while continuing to refresh the current injected plugin runtime. The live QA adapter now derives account-specific replacement paths, preserves configured command owners while authorizing the linked driver, and keeps transport target formatting local to the WhatsApp QA boundary.

Provenance: the runtime-context regression was introduced clearly by #104949, authored and merged by @mcaxtr on July 12, 2026. It became visible when live QA restarted the Gateway during the broadcast fanout scenario.

WhatsApp connections remain available for outbound delivery after plugin registry reloads. Maintainers can run the complete local WhatsApp QA fleet against custom linked account IDs without false config-patch or authorization failures.

target.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway
target.body:
## Summary

- install grouped Claw cron declarations through the gateway-owned `cron.add` API
- persist pending, complete, failed, or removed ownership references keyed by final agent id and declaration id
- expose cron ownership in status, round-trip complete declarations through export, and include exact cron state in remove consent
- disable Claw-owned recurring work before canonical agent deletion, package cleanup, or workspace cleanup
- reuse and extend the canonical agent deletion lifecycle without letting Claws delete unrelated agent files

## Contract

- scheduler mutation stays in the gateway; Claws never write the cron store directly
- declaration keys are scoped as `claw:<agent-id>:<manifest-job-id>`, so package-local ids do not collide globally
- response-lost retries reconcile by declaration key before issuing another `cron.add`
- `main` declarations target `session:agent:<final-agent-id>:main`; `isolated` remains isolated, and strict v1 validation rejects other session modes
- removal calls `cron.remove` before any agent/config mutation and records partial state if recurring work cannot be proven disabled
- canonical `agents.delete` remains responsible for normal agent cleanup; Claws request config/session cleanup while retaining their narrowly managed workspace files for digest-aware removal

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102306 grouped export
- This PR: gateway-owned cron mutation, provenance, status, export, and removal
- Next: #102406 validated MCP ownership

All behavior remains gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- 61 focused cron/lifecycle/schema/provenance/export unit tests
- 15 Claws CLI tests
- 11 canonical agent-delete command tests
- 1 shared agent-cron cleanup test
- 96 gateway agent-mutation tests across gateway projects
- 8 full lifecycle CLI E2E tests
- emitted `cron.add` payload validated by the gateway protocol validator
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across 18 code/generated files
- Oxfmt: all 18 files correctly formatted
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

The lifecycle tests prove consent-bound add, scheduler-id provenance, response-lost reconciliation, status/export visibility, and removal ordering. A scheduler failure returns partial with `agentRemoved: false`; successful removal calls `cron.remove` before either direct config mutation or the canonical agent-delete delegate.

target.title: fix(agents): extract Undici cause.code for ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Undici (Node.js `fetch()` implementation) wraps SocketError (ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT) in a cause chain. The current code in `extractTransportErrorDetails` reads `error.code`, `error.error`, and `error.errorCode`, but misses `error.cause.code` where Undici stores these network error codes.

## Fix
Added `error.cause.code` as the final fallback in `extractTransportErrorDetails` before returning the raw error message. One line changed in production code.

## Changes
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`: One-line addition — reads `error.cause.code` as final fallback, and exports `extractTransportErrorDetails` for testability
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts`: 2 new unit tests
  - Undici cause.code extraction test (simulates real Undici error shape)
  - Priority verification (cause.code checked last, never shadows existing paths)

## Testing
- 24/24 tests passing (agents-core + agents-support)

## Evidence

### Live Undici Error Capture (2026-07-18, Node.js v24.16.0)

Real `fetch()` call to a closed port via Undici:

```json
{
  "name": "TypeError",
  "message": "fetch failed",
  "cause": {
    "code": "ECONNREFUSED",
    "errno": -4078,
    "syscall": "connect"
  }
}
```

**Key observation**: `top-level error.code` is `undefined` on Undici-fetch failures. The error code (`ECONNREFUSED`) is only available at `error.cause.code`. Without this fix, `extractTransportErrorDetails` returns `errorCode: undefined`, and the failover classifier (`classifyFailoverReasonFromCode`) cannot identify the error as a transient network failure.

### Reproduction Script Output

```
REAL UNDICI fetch() ERROR SHAPE VERIFICATION

Test 1: fetch("https://127.0.0.1:19999") -> TypeError: fetch failed
  Top-level code: undefined
  cause.code: ECONNREFUSED
  Fix effective: YES — cause.code is the only source of the error code

Test 2: fetch("https://127.0.0.1:1443") -> TypeError: fetch failed
  Top-level code: undefined
  cause.code: ECONNREFUSED
  Fix effective: YES — same Undici wrapping behavior
```

### Full Error Code Extraction Test

```
6 Undici network error types tested (ECONNRESET, ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, ENOTFOUND, UND_ERR_SOCKET, UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT):
  Before fix: All 6 return errorCode=undefined (failover NOT triggered)
  After fix:  All 6 return correct errorCode (failover correctly triggered as "timeout")

3 non-Undici error types tested:
  All unchanged — priority order preserved
```

### Failover Chain

```
fetch() -> ECONNRESET
  -> Undici wraps: TypeError { message: "fetch failed", cause: { code: "ECONNRESET" } }
  -> extractTransportErrorDetails (before fix): errorCode = undefined
  -> classifyFailoverReasonFromCode(undefined) = null (no failover)
  -> REQUEST FAILS

  -> extractTransportErrorDetails (after fix): errorCode = "ECONNRESET"
  -> classifyFailoverReasonFromCode("ECONNRESET") = "timeout"
  -> Failover to next provider
  -> REQUEST SUCCEEDS
```

## Risk
Extremely low. One-line logic change, new code path only activates when existing fallbacks fail, no existing behavior modified. The `cause.code` path is the last resort in the chain (`errorCode` > `code` > `error.code` > `cause.code`).

target.title: fix(tts-contract): cancel unread response body in OpenAI speech provider
target.body:
## Problem

The OpenAI TTS contract provider in `src/plugins/contracts/tts-contract-suites.ts` calls `fetch()` against `/audio/speech` to validate the request shape but returns a synthetic `audioBuffer` without consuming or cancelling the response body. On keep-alive HTTP connections the unread body holds the socket open until the server closes it, leaking connection slots in contract test runs that exercise `synthesizeSpeech` and `textToSpeechTelephony` repeatedly.

This is the same class of bug as #110574 (TTS live provider body leak) and #110624 (STT live provider body leak), but in the contract suite provider.

## Fix

Capture the `Response`, assert `response.ok`, and `await response.body?.cancel()` before returning so the underlying connection is released. The provider still returns the synthetic buffer — only the cleanup is added.

- Files changed: 1
- LOC delta: +76 / -17

## Regression proof

New `openai provider response body release` suite in `tts-contract-suites.ts` asserts that `body.cancel` is called after both `synthesizeSpeech` and `textToSpeechTelephony`. The shared `withMockedSpeechFetch` helper now returns a mock `body.cancel` so the assertions can be made without a real network socket.

\`\`\`
 ✓ |contracts-plugin| ../../src/plugins/contracts/tts.contract.test.ts (43 tests) 8906ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
\`\`\`

## Risk

Minimal. The fix only adds `response.body?.cancel()` after the existing fetch and an `ok` check that throws on HTTP errors. The synthetic audio buffer returned to callers is unchanged. The only behavioral change is that unread HTTP connections are now released promptly instead of lingering until server timeout.

target.title: fix(agents): route llama.cpp GBNF cleaning through provider tool-schema hooks
target.body:
Fixes #108367
Fixes #108473
Fixes #108580

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw runs against a llama.cpp-backed endpoint with grammar-constrained tool calling, chat requests fail with HTTP 400 before inference whenever the active tool list includes GBNF-hostile JSON Schema constructs (#108580):

1. Unanchored / PCRE-shorthand `pattern` (e.g. `\\S`)
2. `maxLength` above llama.cpp's ~2000 GBNF repetition ceiling (e.g. cron `trigger.script` `65536`)

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical tool schemas keep their server-side validation guidance. Cleaning happens only on llama.cpp-compatible routes:

| Activation path | Who owns it |
|---|---|
| Bundled `ollama`, `ollama-cloud`, `lmstudio`, `llama-cpp` | Provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` via `buildProviderToolCompatFamilyHooks("llamacpp-gbnf")` |
| Custom OpenAI-compatible llama.cpp endpoints | Opt-in `modelCompat.toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` |
| Ordinary providers (`openai`, etc.) | Unchanged — canonical `pattern` / `maxLength` retained |

Shared-core provider-ID guessing was removed (ClawSweeper P1). This mirrors the Gemini family-helper pattern in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-tools`.

## User Impact

llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio users can keep cron and related tools enabled without pre-inference grammar 400s. OpenAI and other providers keep model-facing length/pattern constraints.

## Evidence

### Exact-head bundled-provider live proof (head `71f51dbe274`)

This run registered the real bundled Ollama plugin, selected its provider-owned `normalizeToolSchemas` hook, printed the outbound schema, and sent that schema to a local `llama-server` b9960. Private endpoint details are omitted.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/exact-head-gbnf-live-proof.test.ts --reporter=verbose
EXACT_HEAD=71f51dbe274
PROVIDER_HOOK=ollama
OUTBOUND_SCHEMA={"type":"object","properties":{"declarationKey":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":200},"script":{"type":"string","minLength":1}}}
LLAMA_SERVER_HTTP=200
INFERENCE_RESPONSE={"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"ready"}}],...}

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

This proves the current bundled-provider activation path: `pattern` and oversized `maxLength: 65536` are absent from the outbound schema, `maxLength: 200` remains, and llama-server successfully reaches inference.

### Public contract documentation

The custom-endpoint profile and provider SDK family are documented as supported contracts:

- `docs/gateway/local-models.md`: `compat.toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"`, affected bundled providers, exact cleaning behavior, and ordinary-provider preservation
- `docs/plugins/sdk-provider-plugins.md`: `llamacpp-gbnf` family behavior and bundled examples
- `docs/plugins/sdk-subpaths.md` / `docs/plugins/sdk-migration.md`: public `provider-tools` surface inventory
- `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`: regenerated API contract manifest

### Focused tests
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  packages/ai/src/providers/clean-for-llamacpp-gbnf.test.ts \
  packages/ai/src/providers/agent-tools-parameter-schema.llamacpp.test.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-tools.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/tool-schema-llamacpp-compat.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/index.test.ts \
  extensions/lmstudio/index.test.ts \
  extensions/llama-cpp/index.test.ts
```
All green on Node 22.

### Live llama-server regression transcript (shipped failure)
Earlier local `llama-server` b9960 run against the shipped grammar-hostile cron schema:

- unanchored `\\S` → HTTP 400 `Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`
- `maxLength: 65536` → HTTP 400 `failed to parse grammar`
- cleaned schema (same projection the provider hook now emits) → HTTP 200, inference proceeds

The cleaned payload that reached HTTP 200 is exactly what `normalizeLlamacppGbnfToolSchemas` / `toolSchemaProfile: "llamacpp"` emit on this head.

### vs #108671
#108671 removes constraints from canonical tool schemas globally. This PR preserves them and cleans only on llama.cpp-compatible provider/profile routes — the ownership ClawSweeper recommended.

target.title: fix(feishu): DMs send a spurious no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent NO_REPLY
target.body:
Related: #109912

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users in a direct message (DM) would receive a spurious "⚠️ This reply completed without visible content..." fallback message immediately after the assistant intentionally went silent (emitted only the `NO_REPLY` token). This is confusing and noisy: the assistant correctly decided not to reply, but the user still gets an unwanted message anyway.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's default `blockReplyBreak: "message_end"` setting routes the final assistant text through `sendBlockReply` (dispatch `kind: "block"`), not `sendFinalReply` (`kind: "final"`). When the model's only visible output is `NO_REPLY`, the shared `normalizeReplyPayload` helper correctly detects this as an intentional silent skip and calls `onSkip(payload, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" })`. However, the Feishu dispatcher's `onSkip` handler only ever recorded the skip when `info.kind === "final"`, so `skippedFinalReason` stayed `null` for block-kind silent skips. `ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback` then treated the turn as an ordinary empty response and sent the "no visible content" fallback — a path that is reachable specifically in DMs, where silent finals are disallowed by policy (`src/shared/silent-reply-policy.ts`), and is on for `main`.

The fix widens the `onSkip` condition to also capture block-kind skips whose reason is `"silent"`, matching the intentional-silence signal already produced upstream. It intentionally stays narrow: non-silent block skips (e.g. `reason: "empty"`) still fall through and trigger the fallback exactly as before, so this does not weaken the existing "let the user know nothing came back" safety net for genuinely empty turns.

## User Impact

Feishu DM users who trigger an intentional silent (`NO_REPLY`) response no longer receive a confusing, unwanted "no visible content" fallback message. Behavior for genuinely empty (non-silent) responses is unchanged — those still get the fallback as before.

## Evidence

This PR is AI-assisted (built with Cursor/Claude); I reviewed and understand the change.

### Real dispatch-pipeline proof (added in response to ClawSweeper review)

The strongest evidence in this PR is two tests that drive the **actual production call path** — `createReplyDispatcherWithTyping` → shared `normalizeReplyPayload` → Feishu's real `onSkip` closure — instead of invoking the captured `onSkip` callback directly like the original two tests do. The normalizer decides "NO_REPLY" is silent entirely on its own; nothing about the silent-detection logic is faked. Only the outbound Feishu HTTP calls are mocked, exactly like every other test in this file (there is no live Feishu workspace available in this sandboxed contribution flow to record a literal DM transcript against):

```ts
it("suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  const { result, options } = createDispatcherHarness({ runtime, sessionKey: "main" });
  const { dispatcher } = createReplyDispatcherWithTyping(options);

  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(false);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
});

it("still delivers the fallback for a real genuinely-empty block reply through the full dispatch pipeline", async () => {
  // ...same setup...
  dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "" });
  await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves.toBe(true);

  expect(sendMessageFeishuMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
});
```

Before/after proof for these two tests (reverted the one-line fix, ran them, restored the fix):

Before fix — the positive case fails exactly as the bug predicts, through the real pipeline:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (96 tests | 1 failed | 94 skipped)
    × suppresses the fallback for a real NO_REPLY block reply through the full dispatch pipeline

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2136:72
    dispatcher.sendBlockReply({ text: "NO_REPLY" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete"))...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 94 skipped (96)
```

(The companion "genuinely-empty" test passes even before the fix, confirming it isn't just duplicating the positive case.)

After fix, full file run:

```text
 RUN  v4.1.10 /Users/.../openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  96 passed (96)
```

### Original unit-level proof (invoking the captured onSkip directly)

Before fix (`info.kind === "final"` only), targeted run:

```text
❯ |extension-feishu| ../../extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts (94 tests | 1 failed | 92 skipped)
    × does not send no-visible-reply fallback after an intentional silent block reply

AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
- Expected: false
+ Received: true
 ❯ extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts:2098:72
    options.onSkip?.({ text: "NO_REPLY" }, { kind: "block", reason: "silent" });
    await expect(result.ensureNoVisibleReplyFallback("empty-complete")).resolves...

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 92 skipped (94)
```

### Targeted extension lane

`pnpm test:extension feishu` (85 test files): all Feishu reply-dispatcher tests pass. One unrelated pre-existing failure in `extensions/feishu/src/delivery-trace.test.ts` ("dispatcher options were not captured") reproduces identically on unmodified `upstream/main` before this change — filed separately as #110744 (stale test-capture seam left behind by #110095, which updated the equivalent `msteams`/`slack` tests but missed Feishu's). It is unrelated to `reply-dispatcher.ts`/`reply-dispatcher.test.ts` and is why the `checks-node-changed-*` / `openclaw/ci-gate` check on this PR is currently red — I did not fix it here to keep this PR focused, per `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s guidance on already-broken, unrelated CI:

```text
 Test Files  1 failed | 84 passed (85)
      Tests  5 failed | 1237 passed (1242)
```

target.title: fix(agents): preserve tool-result text when aggregate budget is exhausted (#107704)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #107704
When the aggregate tool-result text budget is fully exhausted and no spill-file markers exist, buildAggregateToolResultReplacements was producing empty strings for ALL tool results. The per-message 1-char floor in clearToolResultText ballooned the effective aggregate budget from N to N × messageCount because each result independently claimed its own 1-char reserve. This caused silent failures on the next model turn — the model sees no content from any tool result.
## Why This Change Was Made
All adjustments are fully gated and preserve existing correct behavior for valid truncation paths:
1. Moved the per-message 1-char floor from clearToolResultText to buildAggregateToolResultReplacements as a single shared aggregate elision reserve, tracked via a hasClaimedElisionReserve flag:
- Only the first eligible tool result without spill markers consumes the 1-char reserve from the global pool
- All subsequent tool results receive 0 reserved characters, eliminating multiplicative budget inflation
- Addedparams.aggregateBudgetChars > 0 guard to ensure zero budget still outputs empty text as expected
2. Refactored ToolResultSpillDetails structure to use flat, explicit field names: fullOutputPath, spillTruncated, spilledChars.
### Behavior: Before vs. After
| Scenario | Before (broken) | After (fixed) |
|----------|-----------------|---------------|
| 50 results × 300 chars, budget = 1 | 50 × 1 char each → 50 chars ❌ | 1 result gets [ → 1 char ✅ |
| 10 results × 100 chars, budget = 0 | 10 × 0 → 0 chars ✅ | 10 × 0 → 0 chars ✅ |
| With spill markers present | Spill pointer preserved | Spill pointer preserved ✅ |

target.title: fix(agents): use raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation for response text fallback
target.body:
## Summary
Replace the post-decode U+FFFD sentinel check with raw-byte fatal UTF-8 validation in `readResponseText`'s `arrayBuffer` fallback path. Malformed bytes are rejected by `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` while legitimate U+FFFD characters (encoded as `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD`) are correctly preserved.

## What Problem This Solves
The previous approach checked `text.includes("�")` after `res.text()` to detect malformed UTF-8. This is incorrect because a server can intentionally send the literal U+FFFD character (`�`) as valid content — the sentinel check would silently discard it. The WHATWG `Response.text()` produces U+FFFD for BOTH cases:
- Malformed byte `0xFF` → silently replaced with `�`
- Valid UTF-8 sequence `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → correctly decoded as `�`

Without raw-byte access, these two cases are indistinguishable from the decoded string alone.

**Code evidence**: [web-shared.ts:300-326](src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts#L300-L326)

## Root Cause
- `Response.text()` uses the WHATWG forgiving UTF-8 decoder — there is no way to opt into fatal mode
- The post-decode U+FFFD check cannot distinguish legitimate U+FFFD from replacement characters
- The `arrayBuffer()` method is available on standard `Response` objects and provides raw bytes

## Why This Fix
When `arrayBuffer()` is available (standard Response), read raw bytes and validate with a two-phase approach:
1. `decodeResponseBytes()` — charset-aware decoder (handles declared charsets)
2. If the result contains `�`, cross-validate: run `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` on the same raw bytes. If it throws → bytes were truly malformed → return empty. If it succeeds → the `�` is a legitimate character → return the decoded text.

When `arrayBuffer()` is not available (mock Response), fall back to `res.text()` without the guard — we cannot distinguish in this case.

## User Impact
- **Before (v1)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` (legitimate U+FFFD) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **compatibility regression**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xEF 0xBF 0xBD` → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "Hi�!" }` — **preserved**
- **After (v2)**: Server sends `0xFF` (malformed) → `readResponseText` returns `{ text: "" }` — **rejected**

## Evidence
- **Legitimate U+FFFD**: strict decode passes → character preserved → **PASS**
- **Malformed bytes**: strict decode throws TypeError → returned empty → **PASS**
- Both cases covered by regression tests

## Real Behavior Proof

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-web-shared-ufffd.mjs
=== Test 1: valid UTF-8 ===
Result: {"text":"Hello, world!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

=== Test 2: malformed UTF-8 bytes (0xFF) ===
Result: {"text":"","truncated":false,"bytesRead":0}
PASS: malformed bytes rejected, returned empty

=== Test 3: legitimate U+FFFD (0xEF 0xBF 0xBD) ===
Result: {"text":"Hi�!","truncated":false,"bytesRead":6}
PASS: legitimate U+FFFD preserved

=== Test 4: text() fallback ===
Result: {"text":"fallback text","truncated":false,"bytesRead":13}
PASS

ALL PASS
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` — 42 passed
- New tests: `returns empty when arrayBuffer provides malformed UTF-8 bytes`, `preserves legitimate U+FFFD when server intentionally sends it`, `returns empty when text() fallback rejects`

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` across canonical agent, workspace, package, session, and scheduled-job state
- bind every remove choice and observed owner/dependency edge into an exact dry-run `planIntegrity` digest
- classify resources consistently as `managed` or `referenced`, with separate origin and current non-Claw owner evidence
- retain referenced resources by default, support safe `--remove-unused`, and support exact repeatable `--remove-referenced <kind:ref@version>` selection
- require `--force-referenced` when a selected resource has another Claw dependent, a non-Claw owner, or pre-existing origin
- invoke canonical skill/plugin removal only after revalidation under the shared cross-process package lifecycle lease

## Scope

This is the authoritative status/remove slice for the experimental one-Claw/one-agent contract. Root and orphaned subordinate provenance are inventoried so missing root rows do not hide recoverable package or workspace state.

Remove is plan-first. Dry-run includes agent identity, config-removal surfaces, bindings, allow entries, scheduled-job blockers, managed-file digests, package relationship/origin/integrity, every known affected Claw, current non-Claw ownership, cleanup mode, filesystem targets, and root state. Apply requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>`, rebuilds the same plan with the same cleanup mode, and fails closed on drift.

Managed resources are cleaned by default when ownership and content are still provable. Referenced resources default to retain/release. `--remove-unused` selects only complete, unchanged, unambiguous, Claw-introduced resources with no other Claw edge or non-Claw owner. `--remove-referenced` selects exact resources; conflicts require the separate `--force-referenced` acknowledgement and remain visible in the plan. A general `--yes` never broadens cleanup.

Ordinary OpenClaw behavior is unchanged. Direct package operations record current independent ownership, ordinary uninstall remains authoritative after Claw-reference warnings, and Claw removal delegates actual mutation to canonical package owners. No refcount or permanent removal tombstone is introduced. Everything remains behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package lifecycle and provenance
- This PR: status, exact remove planning, cleanup choices, canonical removal, and recovery
- Next: #102306 export

## Validation

Exact head: `f683f60b0fb`.

- Node 24.15.0 / SQLite 3.51.3: 47 package/lifecycle/adoption unit tests passed
- Node 24.15.0 / SQLite 3.51.3: 21 Claws CLI tests passed
- focused tests cover default retention, remove-if-unused, exact selected cleanup, conflict override, canonical plugin uninstall, direct-owner adoption, orphan inventory, and digest-bound apply
- scoped Oxfmt and Oxlint passed on all changed files
- GitHub `check-test-types`, `check-prod-types`, max-lines, security, and focused matrix checks pass; final CI is rerunning after two quality-gate fixes
- `git diff --check` passed

## Real behavior proof

The lifecycle E2E invokes the real CLI in isolated state and proves `add -> status -> remove --dry-run -> --yes --plan-integrity` with canonical agent and managed workspace cleanup. Focused exact-head tests additionally execute the canonical plugin-uninstall dependency for selected referenced cleanup and verify that default removal only releases the Claw edge.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where developers running the reusable OpenAI TTS contracts against a custom or local endpoint could wait indefinitely when the endpoint accepted the HTTP request but never returned response headers. Ordinary synthesis and telephony synthesis each had an independent unbounded request path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both contract fixture entry points now share one request helper built on the existing guarded fetch path. The helper applies the caller-provided speech timeout, limits configured-origin trust to the selected base URL hostname, and releases the guarded transport after headers arrive.

The production OpenAI TTS provider already follows this invariant, so this change stays inside the reusable contract fixture and does not change public APIs, configuration, schemas, or provider defaults.

## User Impact

TTS contract runs now fail within a bounded interval when an OpenAI-compatible endpoint stalls before headers, instead of hanging the test process indefinitely. This covers both normal audio synthesis and telephony synthesis.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, the two loopback regressions failed with `ordinary synthesis did not time out` and `telephony synthesis did not time out` against servers that accepted requests but never wrote headers.

## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars
- always assign regenerated exports a derivative package identity and content-derived version
- omit nonportable remote avatars, normalize empty optional arrays, and expand `~` in output paths

## Scope

Export reads the provenance established by the add/status lifecycle and writes a new self-contained package without mutating the installed Claw. It accepts an exact agent id, explicitly projects portable agent fields, copies only ledger-managed workspace files plus a validated local avatar, emits exact recorded package references, and refuses unavailable managed files or an existing output directory.

Image data avatars remain inline. A safe local avatar is read through the pinned workspace avatar boundary, copied under `workspace/`, and rewritten to a workspace-relative manifest path. Remote, missing, or unsafe local avatars are omitted because they are not portable package state.

Every regenerated package is emitted as `openclaw-claw-<agent-id>@0.0.0-export.<content-hash>`, including an unchanged installation. Export never reuses an authenticated publisher's package name/version unless it can return the byte-for-byte original artifact, which this command intentionally does not do.

This slice emits the schema's JSON-compatible representation. The later dedicated #106888 slice changes the canonical exported representation to `CLAW.md` while preserving this package and round-trip behavior.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102296 status/remove and ownership-aware lifecycle state
- This PR: portable creation/export experience
- Next: #102383 gateway-owned cron lifecycle
- Canonical `CLAW.md`: #106888

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across all 6 PR files
- Oxfmt: all 6 PR files correctly formatted
- 8 export unit tests
- 15 Claws CLI tests
- 8 full lifecycle E2E tests
- `git diff --check`
- Codex review: no accepted/actionable findings

## Real behavior proof

The real CLI E2E passes consent-bound add preview/apply -> export -> inspect -> consent-bound add preview/apply from the exported package in isolated state. Export writes `package.json`, `openclaw.claw.json`, managed workspace sidecars, and a portable agent manifest; the fresh add recreates the agent from the derivative package.

target.title: fix(update): dev channel update builds from an unverified checkout at the git install path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Package-to-dev conversion previously adopted whatever Git checkout already existed at `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. A checkout could retain a canonical-looking URL while using `skipFetchAll`, a hostile fetch refspec, a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref, executable local Git config, or URL rewriting to influence what the updater built and globally installed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remote validation cannot make an adopted checkout safe. Package-to-dev conversion therefore requires an unused path, creates a fresh checkout itself, and runs the clone plus all follow-up update/fetch commands with system, global, and injected Git configuration disabled. Existing dev installs still update their own checkout in place; the stricter rule applies only when converting a package install to `dev`.

A conversion that fails after doctor or the global-link step may already have made the new path authoritative, so its checkout has to survive for a retry. Proving that a directory is one the updater created needs two halves: a record the updater controls, and a marker inside the checkout. A marker alone can be planted by a hostile checkout, and a record alone would let a stale entry authorize replacing a checkout somebody else created at that path.

This revision moves that record from a state-directory token file into the shared state database, which is where root `AGENTS.md` requires OpenClaw-owned runtime and recovery state to live. It also fixes the ordering the token file made visible. The record was previously written only after the new checkout was already in place, so an interruption in that window left a checkout whose record and marker disagreed and which the next update then refused. The record is now claimed before the clone runs, the clone lands in a staging directory, the marker is written inside it, and only a fully marked checkout is swapped into place.

## User Impact

- `openclaw update --channel dev` from a package install requires an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`.
- Existing directories, including empty directories and apparently canonical checkouts, are refused.
- The canonical clone and its immediate fetch/build workflow ignore Git config that could rewrite repository selection.
- A conversion interrupted partway can be run again. OpenClaw recognizes the checkout it created at that path and replaces it, rather than refusing its own leftover.
- Removing a checkout OpenClaw created also retires its ownership, so an unrelated directory that later appears at the same path is still refused.
- The interactive wizard and `openclaw update --channel dev` accept exactly the same destinations.
- Existing Git/dev installations are unchanged.

## Regression Coverage

The dedicated checkout suite covers the requested cases with real hostile Git fixtures:

- canonical URL plus `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true` and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a hostile fetch refspec and a seeded `origin/main`;
- canonical URL plus a pre-seeded remote-tracking ref;
- injected/global Git configuration that rewrites the canonical URL;
- existing empty directories;
- clone/update/global-link failures and managed retry replacement.

Interrupted state transitions are covered explicitly:

- an interrupted conversion that reserved its destination but never filled it is reclaimed on retry;
- an interrupted conversion whose destination gained checkout state is refused;
- a completed conversion retires its ownership, so the path is refused again;
- a failed replacement keeps the previous checkout and stays retryable;
- a cleaned-up failed conversion releases ownership, so an unrelated empty directory at that path is still refused;
- the wizard continues a conversion interrupted before its checkout landed.

The command-level suite also verifies refusal occurs before service mutation, follow-up fetches receive the sanitized Git environment, failed initial conversions clean up safely, service-repair-aware failures retain a usable target, and successful conversion retires retry ownership.

## Evidence

Same package-to-dev entrypoint, same pre-seeded canonical-looking checkout, and a byte-identical seeded commit (`cb46fd28`) on both sides. Driven through the real `openclaw update` command path from a package install root (a non-git root, so the updater resolves `installKind: package` and takes the package-to-dev conversion branch). Private paths are replaced with placeholders.

Hostile fixture in both runs: canonical `remote.origin.url`, `remote.origin.skipFetchAll=true`, a pre-seeded `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and a `PAYLOAD.txt` the canonical repository does not contain.

```text
BEFORE (pristine base 7cde0ac8c0) - the existing checkout is adopted
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR config remote.origin.skipFetchAll
true
$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main
cb46fd28114f2f92783c352b390506b416720e7f
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 9999.0.0

Steps:
  OK   clean check (12ms)
  OK   git fetch (15ms)
  FAIL git show-ref main (10ms)
      fatal: 'refs/heads/main' - not a valid ref
  OK   git remote (9ms)
  FAIL upstream check (10ms)
      fatal: no such branch: 'main'
  OK   git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (11ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (20ms)
  OK   preflight checkout (cb46fd28) (12ms)
  OK   preflight deps install (cb46fd28) (402ms)
  FAIL preflight build (cb46fd28) (403ms)
  OK   preflight cleanup (11ms)

Total time: 1.82s
```

There is no `git clone` step: `Root` is the pre-existing directory, so the updater adopted it. `git fetch` reports success in 15ms because the checkout's own `skipFetchAll` suppressed it, and the run then checked out the seeded commit `cb46fd28` and installed dependencies from it. The trailing build failure is only this sandbox lacking a build script for the fixture; the adoption and the checkout of seeded content already happened.

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d, identical inputs) - refused before any mutation
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Error: OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR already exists: <private>/checkout. Package-to-dev conversion
creates a fresh OpenClaw checkout and will not reuse existing directories. Move it or
set OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR to an unused path.
    at reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:249:13)
    at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
  [cause]: Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '<private>/checkout'
      at async reserveGitCheckoutDir (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:243:5)
      at async createGitCheckout (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:295:5)
      at async runGitUpdate (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:456:7)
      at async updateCommandInternal (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:1211:11)
      at async updateCommand (<private>/openclaw/src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts:583:10)
    errno: -17, code: 'EEXIST', syscall: 'mkdir', path: '<private>/checkout'

$ git -C $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR log --oneline -1
cb46fd2 seed hostile checkout
$ ls $OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR
PAYLOAD.txt package.json
```

The refusal comes from the reservation `mkdir` inside `createGitCheckout`, before any step runs against the directory, and the pre-existing checkout is left exactly as it was.

Same head, unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, showing the reordered crash-safe conversion:

```text
AFTER (this patch, head d6d958118d) - fresh path clones for real
$ openclaw update --channel dev --yes
Updating OpenClaw...

Update Result: ERROR
  Root: <private>/unused-checkout
  Reason: preflight-no-good-commit
  Before: 2026.7.2

Steps:
  OK   git clone (174s)
  OK   clean check (1.2s)
  OK   git fetch (824ms)
  OK   upstream check (9ms)
  OK   git rev-parse @{upstream} (10ms)
  OK   git rev-list (12ms)
  OK   preflight worktree (2.79s)
  OK   preflight checkout (a06799ab) (940ms)
  FAIL preflight deps install (a06799ab) (36.36s)
  [9 further preflight checkout / deps install pairs elided; each install failed identically]
  OK   preflight cleanup (3.19s)

Total time: 324.47s
```

Observed while that clone was still running: the destination is reserved but still empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded in the shared state database.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
unused-checkout
$ du -sh <private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout <private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-*
4.0K	<private>/fresh-parent/unused-checkout
124K	<private>/fresh-parent/.unused-checkout.staging-dd7685e9-133e-45fe-893a-95d689fc5329
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
[{"plugin_id":"core:update-cli","namespace":"managed-checkouts","value_json":"{\"token\":\"3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e\",\"dir\":\"<private>/unused-checkout\",\"createdAtMs\":1784258040670}"}]
```

After the staging clone was swapped into place:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ ls -l <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
-rw------- 1 root root 37 Jul 17 03:16 <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
3af8bfdc-0b8e-48ed-bfbb-fd851284582e
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.skipFetchAll; echo "(exit=$?)"
(exit=1)
```

The clone runs into `.unused-checkout.staging-<uuid>` and is swapped into the destination only after it succeeds, leaving no staging directory behind. The ownership token is recorded in the shared state database before the clone starts and matches the `0600` marker written inside the swapped-in `.git`. The fresh checkout carries the canonical remote with no `skipFetchAll` (`git config` exits 1, key unset), and its `git fetch` reaches the network for real (824ms) rather than the adopted checkout's 15ms no-op.

That conversion still ends in `ERROR` because dependency installation cannot run in this sandbox. The failure exercised the recovery path: the updater removed the checkout it had created and retired its ownership record, leaving nothing adopted.

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
$ node -e "... select plugin_id,namespace,value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
(no rows)
```

### Interrupted conversion, then managed replacement (current head)

Driven through the same package-to-dev conversion path on this head, with a real clone of the canonical remote, an isolated state directory, and an unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`. Nothing in `update-cli` is mocked. Two limits on the form of this evidence: the module graph is loaded by the repository's own runner rather than the built launcher, so this is not a shell session transcript; and both runs were stopped deliberately, so the result table the CLI prints when a run ends is absent. What is shown is the on-disk and state-database transitions the recovery path turns on.

A conversion was interrupted with `SIGKILL` at the instant its checkout was swapped into place. Observed while its clone was still running, the destination is reserved but empty, the clone is staged out of place, and ownership is already recorded:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
.unused-checkout.staging-418e65e0-3133-441f-a0a4-d3e96abade95
unused-checkout
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
```

After the kill, the interruption leaves a fully marked checkout whose marker matches the record, and no staging directory:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
233922b5d8b fix(anthropic): accept Claude CLI apiKeyHelper auth (#97492)
```

A sentinel file was then placed inside that leftover checkout so replacement is distinguishable from adoption, and the conversion was run again at the same path. Caught during the swap, the previous checkout is preserved under a backup name until the new one lands:

```text
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
unused-checkout.previous-8cee865a-f8fd-44ee-a655-e14455566026
```

After the replacement:

```text
$ ls <private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt
ls: cannot access '<private>/unused-checkout/INTERRUPTED-SENTINEL.txt': No such file or directory
$ cat <private>/unused-checkout/.git/.openclaw-update-managed
e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde
$ node -e "... select value_json from plugin_state_entries where plugin_id='core:update-cli' ..."
{"token":"e647b160-3cd3-4482-bb5c-8a8bf3e92cde","dir":"<private>/unused-checkout","createdAtMs":1784261913425}
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout log --oneline -1
a0fac37f141 feat: add OpenAI Video Talk (#109579)
$ git -C <private>/unused-checkout config remote.origin.url
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
$ ls -a <private>/fresh-parent
.
..
unused-checkout
```

The sentinel is gone and the commit moved from the leftover's `233922b5d8b` to a freshly cloned `a0fac37f141`, so the retry replaced its own leftover rather than adopting it. The token `e647b160` is reused and `createdAtMs` is unchanged, so the retry recognized existing ownership instead of claiming new ownership over an existing directory. No staging directory and no `.previous-` backup survive the swap.

Not exercised: no successful end-to-end conversion, because dependency installation and the build/global-link steps cannot run in this sandbox; the `global install` step and ownership retirement on the success path were therefore not driven. The interrupted-conversion and managed-replacement flow above was driven through the real conversion path but not through the built launcher as a shell command, and neither of those two runs reached its printed result table.

### Hostile inherited Git template hook (final head)

Driven on final head `16e5d9cae780cebda1e9371e06ec7c30aee7042e` through the real `updateCommand({ channel: "dev", yes: true })` package-to-dev path. The proof used a non-Git package install root, unused `OPENCLAW_GIT_DIR`, isolated state/home, canonical network clone, and inherited `GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR` with an executable `post-checkout`.

An unsafe control clone first executed the hook and created its marker. After removing that marker, the same hostile template was inherited during conversion; execution stopped after the managed checkout landed, then the checkout was inspected. Private paths and machine details are omitted.

```text
proof_head=16e5d9cae780cebda1e9371e06ec7c30aee7042e
package_install_root_git=absent
unsafe_control_hook=executed
conversion_hook_marker=absent
conversion_hook_copied=absent
managed_checkout_marker=present
checkout_remote=https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git
```

The hostile hook neither executed nor copied into the updater-managed checkout; the managed marker and canonical remote establish that the inspected checkout was the updater result. This ran in sanitized AWS Crabbox with public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, and the trusted bootstrap verifying the exact head, isolated HOME, pinned Node/pnpm, and dependencies. The proof exited 0 in 3m52s.

## Validation

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox final-head package-to-dev hook proof: exit 0; redacted transcript above.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/shared.git-checkout.test.ts`: 14 passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli.test.ts`: 188 passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: exit 0.
- `oxlint src/cli/update-cli/ src/infra/errors.ts` and `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- `node --import tsx scripts/check-import-cycles.ts`: 0 runtime value cycles.
- `node scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.mjs`: passed.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

Two failures on the previous head are fixed here rather than carried: `check-lint` rejected an `AggregateError` construction under `preserve-caught-error`, and `update-cli.test.ts` had a wizard case that assumed the pre-existing-path guard did not exist and depended on a fixture directory left behind by earlier runs.
The `createAggregateErrorWithCause` helper lives in a leaf `update-cli` module rather than `src/infra/errors.ts` so the shared plugin-SDK public surface budget stays where it was; `src/infra/errors.ts` is untouched by this PR.

Hosted PR CI is green on this head.

Notes for reviewers:

- Non-test lines grow by roughly 110 against the previous head. That buys the ownership module the storage policy requires plus the staged swap; the alternative was keeping recovery state in a sidecar file.
- Reserving the destination happens immediately before the record is claimed, not after. Claiming first would let the record just written vouch for any empty directory at that path, which would defeat the refusal this PR exists for. The remaining window is one synchronous state write wide, and a crash inside it leaves an empty directory the operator can remove.
- The permanent existing-path policy is still an owner decision and is not settled by this revision.

AI-assisted implementation and review; all final changes were inspected and revised against the repository's contributor and update-safety policies.

## Summary

- Problem: `resolveReservedGatewayMethodScope` and `normalizePluginGatewayMethodScope` are exported pure functions enforcing operator admin scope with 0% test coverage.
- Root cause: No test file existed.
- Fix: Add 10 unit tests covering reserved method prefixes (exec.approvals, config, wizard, update), non-reserved methods, scope coercion, and undefined handling.
- Out of scope: No source changes; test-only addition.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Reserved gateway methods return `operator.admin` scope; non-reserved return undefined.
- Real environment tested: Node.js v22, production functions from `src/shared/gateway-method-policy.js`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: imported via `node --import tsx -e`

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { resolveReservedGatewayMethodScope } from ./src/shared/gateway-method-policy.js"

resolveReservedGatewayMethodScope("exec.approvals.list") → "operator.admin"
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: `levenshteinDistance` computes edit distance between two strings.
- Real environment tested: Node.js v22, production `levenshteinDistance` from `src/shared/levenshtein-distance.js`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: imported the production module via `node --import tsx -e`

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { levenshteinDistance } from ./src/shared/levenshtein-distance.js"

levenshteinDistance("kitten", "sitting") = 3
```

- What was not tested: Performance on strings >1000 characters.

target.title: fix: check channel health after startup grace
target.body:
Closes #105668

## What Problem This Solves

The gateway channel health monitor previously waited for the first full periodic interval before evaluating channels. After the startup grace period ended, an unhealthy channel could therefore remain undetected for up to five additional minutes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run one health check as soon as the startup grace period expires, then arm recurring checks only after that initial check settles. The startup and recurring timers both use the existing single-flight check path and are cleared during stop or shutdown.

The startup grace is also clamped to Node's supported timer range, matching the existing interval normalization.

## User Impact

Unhealthy channels can be detected and recovered immediately after the startup grace window instead of remaining in a blind spot until the first periodic check.

This PR is AI-assisted. I reviewed the implementation and understand the timer and lifecycle changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` — 45 tests passed.
- Focused `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- Project-local autoreview — clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Final head `e8f7f558e807` is merge-updated to `main` `a115af277410`, is mergeable, and still changes only the same three channel-health files (+280/-25).
- The [full final-head Actions suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29648794017) passed: all 30 aggregate CI jobs plus CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, iOS Periphery, macOS Periphery, and Shared OpenClawKit Periphery.

Local validation used Node 24.14, slightly below the repository's Node 24.15 engine floor; CI remains the supported-version proof.

### Patch-identical real Gateway runtime proof

The proof was recorded at `18e88af7e0c940c081214c6029a10861b8db893a`. The final head `e8f7f558e8079b8b5cae705c64678f4722278676` retains byte-identical blobs for all three PR-owned files:

- `channel-health-monitor.integration.test.ts`: `5d83acf9b5af142ff73372613fef020b00dc8a15`

Therefore the Gateway behavior exercised below is byte-identical on the final head.

This proof uses the real Gateway `ChannelManager`, a real channel plugin lifecycle, the production `startChannelHealthMonitor`, and real Node timers. The credential-free probe channel deliberately reports `connected: false`; the manager and timers are not mocked, and fake timers are not used.

target.title: fix(daemon): force killSignal SIGKILL on Windows tasklist PID probe
target.body:
## Problem

`probeProcessState` in `src/daemon/schtasks.ts` calls `spawnSync` on `tasklist.exe` with `timeout: 1_500` but relies on the default `killSignal` (SIGTERM). An unresponsive or hung `tasklist.exe` can ignore SIGTERM, keeping the `spawnSync` blocked past the 1.5s deadline. Since `probeProcessState` is called in a tight loop by `waitForProcessExit` during gateway stop/restart, each stalled probe inflates the polling cycle and can hang doctor/daemon cleanup on Windows.

This is the same class of bug fixed by:
- #109243 (doctor TUI `ps` probe)
- #109731 (gateway pid `ps` probe)

…but the `tasklist.exe` probe in `schtasks.ts` was missed.

## Fix

Force `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` so a stalled `tasklist.exe` is reaped at the deadline instead of hanging the termination path.

- Files changed: 2
- LOC delta: +66 / -1

## Regression proof

New test in `src/daemon/schtasks.stop.test.ts` mocks `process.platform` to `"win32"` and asserts the full `spawnSync` options for `tasklist.exe` include `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`:

\`\`\`
 ✓ |daemon| ../../src/daemon/schtasks.stop.test.ts (21 tests) 977ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
\`\`\`

## Risk

Minimal. Only adds `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to an existing `spawnSync` call that already has a `timeout: 1_500`. On normal Windows hosts where `tasklist.exe` responds within 1.5s, the kill signal is never delivered. The change only affects the abnormal case where the child ignores SIGTERM.

target.title: fix(agents): remove empty parent directory on agent delete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After deleting an agent (via CLI or Gateway), the parent agent state directory
`~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/` is left as an empty folder on disk. Only the
`agent/` and `sessions/` subdirectories are moved to trash; the parent is
never cleaned up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both deletion paths now additionally trash the parent directory after the
subdirectories have been removed:

- **Gateway path** (`agents.delete` handler): calls `moveToTrashBestEffort`
  on `path.dirname(agentDir)` after the existing `Promise.all` for
  subdirectory cleanup.

- **CLI fallback path** (`agentsDeleteCommand`): calls `moveToTrash` on
  `path.dirname(agentDir)` after trashing `agentDir` and `sessionsDir`.

The cleanup is best-effort — if the parent directory is not empty (e.g. other
tooling created files there), the trash operation will fail silently and the
directory is preserved.

## User Impact

No more stale empty directories accumulating under `~/.openclaw/agents/`
after repeated agent create/delete cycles.

## Evidence

### Tests (fail on main, pass on this branch)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agents.delete.test.ts
✓ trashes the parent agent state directory after removing subdirectories

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts
✓ agents.delete > trashes the parent agent state directory after removing subdirectories
```

### Manual verification

```bash
# On main:
$ openclaw agents add test-cleanup
$ openclaw agents delete test-cleanup --force
$ ls ~/.openclaw/agents/test-cleanup/  # directory exists but is empty

# On this branch:
$ openclaw agents add test-cleanup
$ openclaw agents delete test-cleanup --force
$ ls ~/.openclaw/agents/test-cleanup/  # ls: cannot access: No such file or directory
```

target.title: feat(feeds): add local marketplace watches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signed marketplace feeds can be refreshed and inspected, but users cannot durably watch individual entries or review verified changes later. That leaves update awareness as a manual full-catalog comparison.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first client-side watch slice described by the feeds notification plan:

- durable local plugin watches and bounded update history in shared SQLite schema v5
- verified refresh materialization for version/install, removal, blocked, and publisher/security-state changes
- per-watch accepted baselines so unsigned intermediate writes and skipped sequences cannot lose changes
- source binding by feed ID and URL, plus idempotent read/dismiss and functional mute behavior
- `plugins marketplace watch ...` and `plugins marketplace updates ...` operator commands

Only accepted signed plugin feeds can create or advance watches. The schema keeps `item_kind` generic for skills, but this PR does not claim skill watches before a signed skill-feed producer exists.

## User Impact

Users can watch a marketplace plugin, refresh its signed feed normally, list verified local updates, and mark those updates read or dismissed. Muted watches keep their trusted baseline current without producing update events. History is bounded to 500 watches and 500 updates.

This remains local client state. It does not add a hosted inbox, push delivery, polling daemon, or server-side notification service.

## Evidence

- 87 shared-state and schema migration tests
- 53 doctor/state migration tests
- 50 marketplace, signed-feed, and watch-store tests
- 6 lazy CLI routing tests
- generated Kysely schema verification
- type-aware `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`
- `codex review --uncommitted`: clean after addressing event-ID usability, mute semantics, unsigned-baseline continuity, and source isolation

Core `tsgo` was also attempted. Its only branch-owned exhaustive-switch finding was fixed; the remaining diagnostics came from the reused dependency tree being out of sync with this checkout (unrelated missing/older package types).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
A plugin watched from an accepted signed marketplace feed must retain its baseline in local SQLite and materialize a verified update when a newer signed sequence changes that plugin.

Real environment tested:
Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2, Node 24.15.0, PR head `d1c1d82a01a3ab58dc3c3b7bcf2ffc97729572f0`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, a short-lived mutable public JSON HTTPS endpoint serving two DSSE/Ed25519-signed feed revisions, and the real OpenClaw config loader, hosted-feed loader, command handlers, and shared SQLite store. The ephemeral private key remained local with mode 0600 and was deleted after the run; the public fixture was deleted.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Generate an ephemeral Ed25519 key and signed feed sequence 1 containing `proof-plugin` version `1.0.0`.
2. Publish it at `https://jsonblob.com/api/jsonBlob/<redacted>`; configure profile `proof` with the matching public key and `proof-npm` source.
3. Invoke `loadConfiguredHostedOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEntries(loadConfig(), { feedProfile: "proof", timeoutMs: 30000 })` to accept the real HTTPS snapshot. The timeout override was needed because this WSL network exceeded the command's fixed 5-second fetch budget.
4. In a new Node process, invoke `runMarketplaceWatchAddCommand("proof-plugin", { feedProfile: "proof", offline: true, json: true })` against that accepted signed snapshot.
5. In another process, list watches and updates; the watch persisted at sequence 1 and no update existed yet.
6. Replace the bytes at the same HTTPS URL with signed sequence 2, changing the version to `1.1.0`, and invoke the production hosted-feed loader again with the same explicit proof timeout.
7. In another process, invoke the update and watch list command handlers.

Evidence after fix:
```text
accepted sequence 1:
{
  "source": "hosted",
  "feedId": "openclaw-proof-feed-110438",
  "sequence": 1,
  "trust": { "mode": "signed", "signedBy": "proof-root-2026", "signatureCount": 1, "threshold": 1 },
  "entries": [{ "id": "proof-plugin", "version": "1.0.0" }]
}

watch creation:
{
  "created": true,
  "watch": {
    "feedId": "openclaw-proof-feed-110438",
    "feedProfile": "proof",
    "itemKind": "plugin",
    "itemId": "proof-plugin",
    "lastSequence": 1,
    "muted": false
  }
}

separate process before change:
{ "watches": [{ "itemId": "proof-plugin", "lastSequence": 1 }], "count": 1 }
{ "updates": [], "count": 0 }

accepted sequence 2:
{
  "source": "hosted",
  "feedId": "openclaw-proof-feed-110438",
  "sequence": 2,
  "trust": { "mode": "signed", "signedBy": "proof-root-2026", "signatureCount": 1, "threshold": 1 },
  "entries": [{ "id": "proof-plugin", "version": "1.1.0" }]
}

separate process after change:
{
  "updates": [{
    "feedId": "openclaw-proof-feed-110438",
    "itemKind": "plugin",
    "itemId": "proof-plugin",
    "feedSequence": 2,
    "reason": "updated",
    "title": "Signed Feed Proof Plugin",
    "itemVersion": "1.1.0",
    "itemState": "available"
  }],
  "count": 1
}
{ "watches": [{ "itemId": "proof-plugin", "lastSequence": 2 }], "count": 1 }
```

Observed result after fix:
The real HTTPS feed was accepted only after Ed25519 verification, the watch survived independent process restarts in shared SQLite, sequence 1 produced no false update, and signed sequence 2 produced exactly one persisted `updated` event for version `1.1.0` while advancing the watch baseline to sequence 2.

What was not tested:
The packaged/full CLI bootstrap was not used because its source launcher did not reach the action in this checkout within 30 seconds; exported production command handlers were invoked directly. The network loader used a 30-second proof timeout rather than the command's fixed 5-second timeout. Skill watches remain intentionally unsupported. Shared SQLite v5 ownership and downgrade policy still require explicit core maintainer acceptance before merge.
